**Product Description Text**:
> The MCP TypeScript SDK is the official implementation of the Model Context Protocol, providing a standardized way for applications to supply context to large language models by separating context provisioning from LLM interaction. It ships split packages for building both MCP servers (`@modelcontextprotocol/server`) and MCP clients (`@modelcontextprotocol/client`), supporting tools, resources, prompts, and transports including Streamable HTTP and stdio, along with OAuth helpers. The SDK runs on Node.js, Bun, and Deno, and uses Standard Schema for tool and prompt validation, enabling compatibility with Zod v4, Valibot, ArkType, and other schema libraries. Optional middleware packages offer thin adapters for popular web frameworks, including Express, Fastify, Hono, and Node's built-in HTTP module, with no added MCP functionality beyond wiring. It is currently on the v2 stable release line implementing the 2026-07-28 MCP specification, with comprehensive documentation, tutorials, and runnable examples to help developers build both servers and clients, and is licensed under Apache 2.0.

> uniTerm is a lightweight, all-in-one terminal client that consolidates 30+ connection protocols into a single cross-platform application, eliminating the need for separate tools for SSH, RDP, SFTP, databases, and container management. It supports terminal access (SSH, Telnet, Mosh, serial, local shells, WSL), file transfer (SFTP, SCP, FTP, SMB, WebDAV, S3, Zmodem), remote desktop (RDP, VNC, SPICE, X11), databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, MongoDB, Elasticsearch), and container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker, Podman). A built-in autonomous AI Agent plans and executes multi-turn shell commands directly in active terminal tabs, with configurable safety modes, persistent conversation history, and integration with Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs. The application features split panes, customizable keybindings, 28 terminal themes, 9-language UI localization, and encrypted cloud sync via private GitHub, GitLab, or Gitee repositories. uniTerm is aimed at DevOps engineers, system administrators, and developers who manage diverse remote infrastructure and want a unified, keyboard-driven workspace. The project is built primarily in Go (with Rust components for select drivers) using Tauri for its cross-platform desktop frontend, and is available under an open-source license with releases on GitHub and Gitee.

It solves the problem of fragmented agent workflows by providing durable sessions, persistent context, and finished artifacts (documents, spreadsheets, code changes) that teams can actually use. > Vaultisse is an open-source web application for cataloging and managing physical book collections in homes, school libraries, or small lending libraries. It tracks each book's location, loan status, and full metadata (author, category, language, format, cover), while also allowing users to automatically retrieve book details by ISBN through the Google Books API, with Open Library and LibraryThing as fallbacks for cover images. The platform supports tracking individual physical copies independently, maintaining a borrower directory, organizing books by shelf location, printing barcode labels, and providing full-text search along with dashboard statistics and charts. It is built as a Vue 3 single-page application with Vuetify on the frontend, communicating with a Node.js/Express/TypeScript REST API backed by PostgreSQL on the backend, with the server serving the built client in production as a single process. Security is handled through cookie/session-based JWT authentication, bcrypt password hashing, optional OIDC/SSO integration, rate limiting, and secure HTTP headers, while the interface is localized in English, Spanish, Catalan, and Italian. The application is ideal for librarians, educators, book collectors, and small organizations seeking a self-hostable alternative to commercial library management systems, with Docker and PM2 deployment options included.

It is designed to be forked: users clone the repository, point it at their own Supabase project and Meta credentials, and deploy anywhere Node.js runs — with Hostinger's managed Node.js hosting recommended for one-click deployment. Core features include a multi-agent shared inbox with assignment and notes, Kanban-style deal pipelines, CSV contact imports with deduplication, Meta-approved broadcast templates with delivery tracking, a visual automation builder (triggers, branches, waits, webhooks), and an AI reply assistant powered by the user's own OpenAI or Anthropic key — optionally grounded in a knowledge base via Postgres full-text or pgvector retrieval. #### 1. [supabase](https://github.com/supabase/supabase) (`supabase/supabase`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/supabase/supabase](https://github.com/supabase/supabase)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://supabase.com](https://supabase.com)
- **Primary Language**: `TypeScript` | **Stars**: `★ 107,342` | **License**: `Apache-2.0`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *ManuAGI - AutoGPT Tutorials* | Video: *Top Dev Tool Projects : Claude Code, Supabase, Anki, rustfs, GitDiagram & OpenSpec* | Published: *2026-09-24*
- **Attached Keywords**: `security, database, postgresql, ai`
- **GitHub Topics**: `ai, alternative, auth, database, deno, embeddings, example, firebase, nextjs, oauth2, pgvector, postgis, postgres, postgresql`

**Product Description Text**:
> The open source Firebase alternative. Supabase gives you a dedicated Postgres database to build your web, mobile, and AI applications.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform that provides a Firebase-like developer experience for building web, mobile, and AI applications. It combines enterprise-grade tools—including a hosted PostgreSQL database, PostgREST for auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, GoTrue for JWT-based authentication, realtime websocket subscriptions, S3-compatible file storage, edge functions, and a vector/embeddings toolkit for AI workloads. Developers can use it as a managed cloud service or self-host it locally, with modular client libraries available for JavaScript, Flutter, Swift, and other languages. The platform is aimed at developers seeking a scalable, relational backend without vendor lock-in, leveraging Postgres as its foundation. Community support is provided through GitHub Discussions, Discord, and dedicated issue tracking, while an intuitive dashboard simplifies database management and configuration.


#### 2. [Deep-Live-Cam](https://github.com/hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam) (`hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam](https://github.com/hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://deeplivecam.net/](https://deeplivecam.net/)
- **Primary Language**: `Python` | **Stars**: `★ 94,297` | **License**: `AGPL-3.0`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *ManuAGI - AutoGPT Tutorials* | Video: *Top Dev Tool Projects : Langfuse, Shannon, Temporal, OpenMetadata & CodeBurn* | Published: *2026-04-23*
- **Attached Keywords**: `python, video, ai`
- **GitHub Topics**: `ai, ai-deep-fake, ai-face, ai-webcam, artificial-intelligence, deep-fake, deepfake, deepfake-webcam, faceswap, fake-webcam, gan, real-time-deepfake, realtime, realtime-deepfake`

**Product Description Text**:
> real time face swap and one-click video deepfake with only a single image (uncensored)

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Deep-Live-Cam enables real-time face swapping and one-click video deepfake creation using just a single source image, eliminating the need for extensive training data or complex model preparation. The tool supports live webcam feeds as well as pre-recorded video processing, making it accessible for streaming, content creation, and entertainment purposes such as creating personalized movie experiences, memes, or live performances. Key features include a Mouth Mask function to preserve natural lip movement, multi-face mapping for swapping different faces onto multiple subjects simultaneously, and built-in content moderation checks that block nudity, graphic material, and sensitive footage before processing. The project provides optimized pre-built binaries for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), and CPU-only environments, with optional GPU acceleration through CUDA for Nvidia hardware. It targets content creators, streamers, meme artists, and developers in the AI-generated media industry while requiring GPU support (NVIDIA/AMD/Apple Silicon) for optimal real-time performance. The tech stack leverages ONNX-based face-swapping models (inswapper_128_fp16), GFPGANv1.4 for face enhancement, PyTorch, and ONNX Runtime execution providers, with Python 3.14 as the recommended runtime.


#### 3. [awesome-design-md](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md) (`VoltAgent/awesome-design-md`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://github.com/VoltAgent/voltagent](https://github.com/VoltAgent/voltagent)
- **Primary Language**: `Not specified` | **Stars**: `★ 93,801` | **License**: `MIT`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Github Awesome* | Video: *GitHub Trending monthly #62026.04* | Published: *2026-05-01*
- **Attached Keywords**: `ai, web, design, markdown, tools`
- **GitHub Topics**: `awesome-list, design-md, design-system, design-tokens, figma, google-stitch, landing-page, vibe-coding, vibe-design, vibecoding`

**Product Description Text**:
> A collection of DESIGN.md files analysis by popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Awesome DESIGN.md is a curated collection of plain-text design system documents extracted from real-world brand websites, covering AI platforms, developer tools, databases, productivity apps, and creative tools. Each DESIGN.md captures analyzed design tokens, typography, color palettes, spacing rules, and component patterns from brands like Vercel, Linear, Supabase, Notion, Cursor, and dozens more. Developers drop the file into their project root and instruct an AI coding agent to generate UI that visually matches the chosen brand's design language — no Figma exports or JSON schemas required. The concept builds on Google's Stitch DESIGN.md format, leveraging markdown as a format that LLMs parse natively for consistent, high-quality output. **Product Description Text**:
> The realtime client-side database

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Instant is a backend platform designed for AI-coded applications, providing auth, permissions, storage, presence, and streams out of the box. At its core is a client-side relational database that eliminates the need for separate stores, selectors, endpoints, and local caches by allowing developers to write queries in the shape of the data they want, known as InstaQL. Every query is multiplayer by default, with built-in support for optimistic updates, rollbacks, offline caching via IndexedDB, and ephemeral features like cursors and online status. Under the hood, Instant stores all data as triples in a multi-tenant Postgres database, uses a Clojure-based sync server that tails Postgres' WAL for real-time invalidation, and enforces data access through Google's CEL permission library. It ships with SDKs for JavaScript, React, and React Native, making it ideal for developers who want to ship full-featured, real-time apps without managing traditional backend infrastructure.

> DeepGEMM is a high-performance CUDA library that provides optimized tensor core kernels for the core computation primitives in modern large language models, including FP8/FP4/BF16 GEMMs, fused MoE operations, and MQA scoring. It solves the challenge of efficiently running low-precision and specialized kernels on NVIDIA Hopper (SM90) and Blackwell (SM100) GPUs, while keeping the codebase small and accessible for learning GPU optimization techniques. The library employs runtime JIT compilation via DeepJIT, eliminating the need for CUDA compilation during installation, and draws inspiration from CUTLASS and CuTe without inheriting their heavy template complexity. DeepGEMM achieves up to 1550 TFLOPS on H800 GPUs and matches or exceeds expert-tuned libraries across diverse matrix shapes, supporting both dense and grouped GEMMs (contiguous and masked layouts) as well as advanced features like Mega MoE, HyperConnection, sparse indexers, and PDL. It targets ML engineers and researchers working on LLM training and inference who need efficient low-precision matrix operations, with a Python interface backed by PyTorch 2.3+ and CUDA Toolkit 12.9+.

It solves the problem of needing scalable, low-latency pub/sub messaging with features beyond Pusher's offering, including message recovery, rewind, durable history, mutable messages, presence tracking, annotations, and tag filtering. It includes first-party client SDKs for JavaScript, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, .NET, and Python, along with server-side SDKs for backend publishing, and an optional AI Transport built on the same primitives for streaming AI workloads. Sockudo is intended for developers and teams requiring realtime features—chat, notifications, live updates, collaborative apps, or AI streaming—who want Pusher compatibility without vendor lock-in, or who need richer semantics like message versioning, idempotent publishing, and two-tier recovery. Deployment is flexible, with Docker Compose, Helm charts, Prometheus metrics, webhooks, rate limiting, and TLS support for production use.

> Sakura Crossing is a fully explorable 3D neighbourhood in Three.js that renders to look like a hand-painted 2D anime background, solving the challenge of producing a cel-shaded look without any image assets. Every sign, lantern, and shop fascia is drawn at runtime with Canvas2D, while the "anime" aesthetic comes from four layered techniques: quantised toon lighting with a hue-shifted shadow ramp, a screen-space second-difference depth ink pass, inverted-hull outlines on key props, and a two-light setup with split-tone colour grading. The world is a small planet centred on a Japanese level crossing and grows outward to include a shopping street, shrine, high school, residential lanes, a festival ground, and a railway that loops the entire globe; the scene is deliberately unpopulated, letting detritus and signage carry the atmosphere. Twenty-two interactables respond to the `E` key, including nineteen vending machines that dispense cans and a relay box that calls a train (which otherwise arrives every 35–45 seconds), and a coral-painted e-bike can be summoned for fast traversal. Built with three.js and Vite as the only dependencies, it runs on any Node 18+ setup and targets developers and graphics enthusiasts interested in non-photorealistic rendering pipelines for anime-style real-time scenes.

**Product Description Text**:
> Syncular is an offline-first data synchronization framework that keeps an SQLite database on each client and reconciles changes through a server-owned commit log, enabling apps to read locally and continue working without connectivity. Writes update local state immediately, enter an outbox, and are validated by the server during sync, with a formally specified wire protocol verified by shared byte-level conformance tests across both TypeScript and Rust cores. The browser client uses SQLite on OPFS, while native platforms—Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, and Tauri—share the Rust core and native SQLite bindings. Servers run on Bun, Node, or Cloudflare Workers and support SQLite, Postgres, or D1 storage backends. Optional packages provide Yjs CRDT integration, column-level encryption, schema/query code generation for multiple languages, React hooks, and an in-process testkit for deterministic fault-injection testing. It targets developers building offline-capable, multi-platform applications who need reliable local-first storage with conflict-free replication without giving up SQL.

> Firemigrate: open-source CLI moving Firebase data to PostgreSQL ('Inspect first. Write last.'), `npx @ezekielreu6/firemigrate`; read-only inspection, schema preview, dry runs by default. GH: 2★.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> FireMigrate migrates data from Firebase Firestore (collections and nested subcollections), Firebase Authentication users, and Firebase Storage object metadata into PostgreSQL, making it a practical bridge for teams moving from Firebase to Supabase or any Postgres-based backend. It is safe by default: every operation runs as a dry run unless `--write` is passed alongside `dryRun: false`, and re-running is idempotent because rows are upserted by document id. Schema inference samples documents and routes unexpected fields into a `_extra` JSON column so later additions are not lost, while subcollections are discovered by walking parent documents up to 20 levels deep and flattened into namespaced tables like `users__posts__comments`. The CLI also exposes an agent-friendly `tables` command that emits a JSON manifest of destination tables for downstream automation, and an optional hash-mode rebuild of Firebase password hashes into `$fbscrypt$` form for later Supabase Auth import. The tool is written in TypeScript/Node.js (run via `npx` or `pnpm`), targets PostgreSQL 14+ through `DATABASE_URL`, and is aimed at developers and platform engineers performing one-time Firebase-to-Postgres cutovers.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> FlashAttention is a fast, memory-efficient implementation of exact attention that uses an IO-aware tiling strategy to minimize memory reads/writes between GPU HBM and SRAM, dramatically reducing the memory and computational cost of transformer attention. It provides official implementations of FlashAttention, FlashAttention-2, a beta FlashAttention-3 optimized for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs (with FP16/BF16 and FP8 forward support), and FlashAttention-4 written in CuTeDSL for Hopper and Blackwell architectures. > The open source Firebase alternative. Supabase gives you a dedicated Postgres database to build your web, mobile, and AI applications.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform that provides a Firebase-like developer experience for building web, mobile, and AI applications. It combines enterprise-grade tools—including a hosted PostgreSQL database, PostgREST for auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, GoTrue for JWT-based authentication, realtime websocket subscriptions, S3-compatible file storage, edge functions, and a vector/embeddings toolkit for AI workloads. Developers can use it as a managed cloud service or self-host it locally, with modular client libraries available for JavaScript, Flutter, Swift, and other languages. The platform is aimed at developers seeking a scalable, relational backend without vendor lock-in, leveraging Postgres as its foundation. Community support is provided through GitHub Discussions, Discord, and dedicated issue tracking, while an intuitive dashboard simplifies database management and configuration.

It transforms any existing SQL database into a no-code platform, enabling teams to create, read, update, and delete tables, columns, and rows with operations like sorting, filtering, grouping, and hiding columns. The platform supports multiple view types including Grid, Gallery, Form, Kanban, and Calendar, along with features like collaborative views, access controls, and automations. NocoDB is easy to deploy via Docker, with support for SQLite or PostgreSQL backends, and includes a one-command "Auto-upstall" option that provisions the full stack (PostgreSQL, Redis, Traefik, SSL) for production use. **Product Description Text**:
> DuckDB is an analytical in-process SQL database management system

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> DuckDB is a high-performance analytical in-process SQL database management system designed for fast, efficient Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) workloads directly within applications. It solves the problem of needing a lightweight yet powerful analytical engine without the overhead of a separate database server, making it ideal for data scientists, analysts, and developers working with large datasets. DuckDB features a rich SQL dialect supporting advanced capabilities such as window functions, arbitrary correlated subqueries, complex types (arrays, structs, maps), and user-friendly SQL extensions. It provides seamless data import from CSV and Parquet files simply by referencing them in queries, eliminating complex ETL steps. The system is accessible via a standalone CLI and offers robust client integrations for Python (including dplyr-style APIs), R, Java, and WebAssembly, with native compatibility with pandas and dplyr. Built in C++17, DuckDB requires CMake and Python 3 for development, offering optimized columnar execution, reliability, and cross-platform portability.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> SurrealDB is a scalable, distributed, multi-model database written in Rust that unifies document, graph, relational, time-series, geospatial, and key-value data types into a single engine. It eliminates the need for most server-side components by combining database and API backend functionality, including real-time live queries, WebSocket connections, end-user authentication, and granular row-level permissions. The database supports SQL-like querying through SurrealQL, as well as GraphQL, ACID transactions, full-text and vector indexing, and graph traversal without JOINs. It can be deployed as a single Rust binary running embedded in applications, in the browser via WebAssembly, at the edge, self-hosted, or scaled across distributed clusters in the cloud. Developers building AI agent data layers, knowledge graphs, recommendation engines, fraud detection systems, and other data-intensive applications use SurrealDB to simplify infrastructure and accelerate development. The project offers official client libraries for JavaScript, Python, .NET, PHP, and more, plus an MCP server for LLM integration.

**Product Description Text**:
> Bramble is a local-first, end-to-end encrypted password manager that keeps user vaults stored on personal devices rather than on company servers, eliminating the risk of third-party breaches. It solves the trust problem inherent to cloud-based password managers by syncing vaults directly between a user's own devices via a private peer-to-peer mesh, with no relay server holding plaintext data. The platform supports Chromium browsers and Firefox via an extension, plus native iOS and Android apps featuring system AutoFill, biometric unlock (Face ID, Touch ID, Android biometrics), and passkey support. All cryptographic operations run in a shared Rust core compiled to WebAssembly on desktop and as a native library on mobile, using Argon2id key derivation, AES-256-GCM encryption, and per-entry envelope encryption, with secrets wiped from memory after use. Beyond syncing, Bramble offers multiple backup strategies, including encrypted `.bramble` file exports, KeePass `.kdbx` exports, and scheduled ciphertext-only backups to Dropbox, S3-compatible storage, or self-hosted WebDAV. It is aimed at privacy-conscious users and self-hosters who want full control over their credentials without vendor lock-in.

- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Github Awesome* | Video: *GitHub Trending Weekly #41: canvas-ui, openworker, thinking-orbs, no-ai-slop, sticker-forge, justif* | Published: *2026-07-25*
- **Attached Keywords**: `sqlite, database, tools, rust`

**Product Description Text**:
> minisqlite is a from-scratch reimplementation of SQLite written in Rust, providing a full SQL database engine with parser, query planner and executor, transactions, and a storage engine that reads and writes SQLite's official on-disk file format. It exposes a deliberately minimal public API consisting of a single `Connection` type with four methods (`open`, `open_in_memory`, `execute`, `query`), plus the `Value`, `Row`, and `Error` types, making it suitable for embedding in Rust applications that need SQLite-compatible persistence without linking against the C library. The implementation spans roughly 200,000 lines across 14 layered crates covering the SQL dialect (including joins, CTEs, window functions, upserts, generated columns, triggers, and foreign keys), about 90 built-in functions, ~20 PRAGMAs, WAL and rollback-journal modes, and ~5,650 tests. It uses only one external dependency (`elsa`, for the page cache) and contains no `unsafe` code in library code, making it attractive for projects that prioritize memory safety and a small dependency surface. The intended audience includes systems programmers, database researchers, and developers who need a verifiable, auditable, format-compatible SQL engine in pure Rust.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> redis-lua-py lets developers write Redis Lua scripts as native Python functions instead of opaque strings, addressing the common pain points of editor highlighting, linting, and type checking being unavailable in traditional string-based Lua definitions. At import time, the library parses a restricted Python subset, compiles it into Lua, checks Redis command names against the official command table, and dispatches the result with `EVALSHA` (or `FCALL` for Redis Functions), producing a stable hash that makes the server's script cache cold only once per script. Scripts support typed parameters where annotated `Key` arguments become `KEYS` for Cluster routing, `int`/`float` values are wrapped in `tonumber`, module-level constants are folded in as literals, and `bytes` values pass through unchanged without decoding. It works with both sync and async clients from redis-py 4.2+ and coredis, and exposes the generated Lua on each script for code review and golden-file testing. A `python -m redis_lua_py generate` command emits a standalone module of typed functions with no runtime dependency on the package, and a `--check` flag keeps generated code in sync during CI.

#### 1. [firecrawl](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl) (`firecrawl/firecrawl`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev)
- **Primary Language**: `TypeScript` | **Stars**: `★ 158,765` | **License**: `AGPL-3.0`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *ManuAGI - AutoGPT Tutorials* | Video: *Top Dev Tool Projects : Playwright, Firecrawl, Temporal, LikeC4, Kimi Code CLI & Strix* | Published: *2026-07-30*
- **Attached Keywords**: `ai, ai-agents, mcp, web, markdown, llm`
- **GitHub Topics**: `ai, ai-agents, ai-crawler, ai-scraping, ai-search, crawler, data-extraction, html-to-markdown, llm, markdown, scraper, scraping, web-crawler, web-data`

**Product Description Text**:
> Firecrawl is an open-source API designed to power AI agents by providing reliable methods for searching, scraping, and interacting with the web at scale. It specializes in extracting clean, structured data from complex web pages, including handling JavaScript-heavy content and managing proxy issues automatically. The service offers features such as web search, comprehensive scraping, and advanced interaction capabilities like clicking and scrolling. Firecrawl ensures LLM-ready output, delivering data in formats like markdown, JSON, and screenshots, which significantly reduces token usage for AI applications. Built for speed and reliability, it acts as a crucial data layer, enabling AI agents to gather and process real-time web information efficiently.


#### 2. [iptv](https://github.com/iptv-org/iptv) (`iptv-org/iptv`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/iptv-org/iptv](https://github.com/iptv-org/iptv)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://iptv-org.github.io](https://iptv-org.github.io)
- **Primary Language**: `TypeScript` | **Stars**: `★ 128,833` | **License**: `Unlicense`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *ig_scraper* | Video: *IG Scraper Links* | Published: *2026-09-23*
- **Attached Keywords**: `streaming`

**Product Description Text**:
> IPTV, open database of IPTV channels. IPTV is an open source repository that maintains a large collection of publicly available IPTV channel playlists

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> A community-maintained repository aggregating publicly available IPTV channels from around the world into curated M3U playlists that can be loaded directly into any compatible video player like VLC. Users can access a master playlist containing all channels or browse categorized playlists via the PLAYLISTS.md file, while an Electronic Program Guide (EPG) is available through a companion repository. Channel metadata is sourced from a separate structured database, and developers can interact with the data via a dedicated REST API. The project serves cord-cutters, IPTV app developers, and researchers needing an organized catalog of free, publicly broadcast stream URLs. No video files are hosted; the repository only collects and links to stream sources that copyright holders have intentionally published openly. Licensed under CC0, it includes built-in processes for handling copyright claims and welcomes community contributions for adding or correcting channels.


#### 3. [ragflow](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow) (`infiniflow/ragflow`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://ragflow.io](https://ragflow.io)
- **Primary Language**: `Go` | **Stars**: `★ 88,680` | **License**: `Apache-2.0`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Cooly* | Video: *Cooly's Chrome Links* | Published: *2026-09-02*
- **Attached Keywords**: `retrieval-augmented-generation, ai-agents, context-management, open-source, rag, llm`
- **GitHub Topics**: `agent-harness, agentic-ai, agentic-retrieval, agentic-search, ai, ai-agents, context-engine, context-engineering, context-management, harness-engineering, knowledge-compilation, llm-apps, rag, retrieval-augmented-generation`

**Product Description Text**:
> RAGFlow is an open-source RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) engine based on deep document understanding.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> RAGFlow is an open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation engine that combines advanced RAG capabilities with Agent functionality to deliver high-quality context for large language models. It addresses the challenge of extracting reliable, grounded answers from complex unstructured data by providing deep document understanding, template-based chunking, and traceable citations that reduce hallucinations. The platform supports a wide range of data sources including Word, Excel, PDF, images, scanned documents, and web pages, while offering configurable LLM and embedding model integration with fused re-ranking for improved retrieval accuracy. Developers and enterprises can leverage its streamlined RAG orchestration, agentic workflows, MCP support, and pre-built agent templates to build production-ready AI systems with minimal complexity. Deployment is flexible, with options including a hosted cloud service, Docker images, and self-hosting via source code. The stack is Python-based (3.13+) and designed to scale from individual projects to large enterprise deployments.


#### 4. [browser-use](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use) (`browser-use/browser-use`)

- **Attached Keywords**: `automation, ai-agents, python, agent, cli, web, playwright, llm`
- **GitHub Topics**: `ai-agents, ai-tools, browser-automation, browser-use, llm, playwright, python`

**Product Description Text**:
> Make websites accessible for AI agents

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Browser-use makes websites accessible to AI agents by enabling them to interact with browsers the same way humans do—opening pages, clicking buttons, typing text, and filling out forms through simple natural-language task prompts. It solves the problem of web automation for AI by offering both an open-source Python library for developers and a CLI skill that any AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) can install to gain browser capabilities. It provides reliable, scalable table storage with full transactional support, enabling concurrent reads and writes, schema enforcement, and time travel on data stored in formats like Parquet. The framework integrates seamlessly with major compute engines including Apache Spark, PrestoDB, Trino, Apache Flink, and Apache Hive, and offers APIs for Scala, Java, Rust, Ruby, and Python. Underlying storage systems must provide atomic visibility, mutual exclusion, and consistent listing to maintain Delta Lake's ACID guarantees. Backward compatibility is guaranteed across versions, while forward compatibility may be broken as the transaction protocol evolves with new features. Data engineers and platform teams building large-scale analytics, ETL, and streaming pipelines use Delta Lake to unify batch and streaming workloads on a single, reliable storage layer.

**Product Description Text**:
> High-performance retrieval engine for unstructured data

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> dsRAG is a high-performance retrieval engine designed for unstructured data, particularly excelling at complex queries over dense, lengthy documents like financial reports, legal filings, and academic papers. It addresses the limitations of vanilla RAG systems—which struggle with questions requiring synthesis across multiple text sections—by introducing three core techniques: semantic sectioning, AutoContext, and Relevant Segment Extraction (RSE). Semantic sectioning uses an LLM to partition documents into coherent segments with descriptive titles, while AutoContext prepends document- and section-level metadata to chunks before embedding, dramatically improving retrieval precision. Relevant Segment Extraction clusters related chunks at query time and intelligently reassembles them into longer, contextually complete segments tailored to the question. The library supports multiple vector databases including Faiss, Chroma, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, and Pinecone, and is installable via pip with optional dependency groups. Benchmarks demonstrate substantial accuracy gains, achieving 96.6% on FinanceBench compared to 32% for vanilla RAG, and an average score improvement from 4.72 to 8.42 on the KITE benchmark. It is well-suited for AI engineers and developers building production-grade RAG applications where retrieval quality over complex document corpora is critical.

The converter uses a three-stage pipeline built on Pandoc 3.x with Lua 5.4 filters for the heavy lifting, wrapped by Python for repository management and output formatting. Users can convert any standard version via git tags, branches, or SHAs, with pre-converted versions already available for C++11 (n3337) through C++26 (trunk). The tool supports multiple modes including single-file output, separate chapter files with automatic cross-link fixing, and version diff generation for HTML site builds. It targets C++ developers, committee members, language lawyers, and educators who need accessible, searchable versions of the standard, and is released into the public domain under the Unlicense.

A successful read produces a small JSON "reading spec" describing the layout, so subsequent invoices of the same shape are processed in milliseconds with no model call and no network access. Accountants, finance teams, AP automation developers, and anyone who needs to convert varied PDF invoices into trustworthy structured data benefit most, since the tool detects tampering or OCR mistakes via built-in cross-foot checks and returns unproven reads with the failed check rather than silently producing wrong totals. Built on Node.js 20+ as an ES module package, it exposes a CLI (`crossfoot invoice.pdf`) and a programmatic API (`createReader`), with pluggable model adapters (Anthropic supported) and pluggable spec stores. Output preserves the document's original text formatting for numbers and dates, names columns after the headings printed on the page, and returns a typed result with `proven`, `rows`, `via`, and `problem` fields so callers can decide how to handle unproven documents.

> RE:Dox is a high-performance, token-based structured data engine for .NET that parses JSON, JSON5, CBOR, MessagePack, TOML, XML, HTML, CSV, INI, and DOX into a compact, fixed-size 64-bit token DOM/IR, serving as a shared structural layer for reading, editing, format conversion, and serialization. It addresses the typical trade-off between parse speed (tape DOM), editability (node DOM), and flexibility (Newtonsoft-style `$type`/`$id`/`$ref` references) by unifying all three into a single mutable token representation. Benchmarks against System.Text.Json show up to ~1.8x faster sequential deserialization, up to ~2.8x faster automatic parallel deserialization, and up to ~1.6x faster serialization, with significantly lower allocations (e.g., 2.56 MB vs 8.53 MB for `canada.json`). The library includes format-agnostic `DataReader`/`DataWriter` abstractions, trivia-preserving JSON5 editing, and compatibility shims for System.Text.Json, Newtonsoft.Json, and DataContractJsonSerializer, all under an Apache-2.0 license. It is developed as a core component of CAPCOM's "REX" next-generation game engine technology. Target users are .NET developers and game engine teams needing a fast, editable, multi-format structured data layer for high-performance scenarios.

> ZenConverter is a local-first file conversion app for Android that addresses the lack of clean, ad-free, privacy-respecting converter tools on the platform. It performs all conversion work directly on-device, requiring no network transfer for file processing and deliberately omitting ads, accounts, paywalls, and remote uploads; the `INTERNET` permission is restricted to manual update checks and on-demand model or font downloads. The app supports a wide range of formats, including video conversion and merging via FFmpeg, audio extraction, image format conversion, image super-resolution using both bilinear and Real-ESRGAN deep-learning models, PDF tools, office document conversion, font conversion (TTF, OTF, WOFF, WOFF2), and subtitle/lyrics format conversion. Advanced features such as video frame interpolation, video overview contact sheets, animated GIF export, and metadata safety inspection are included, with each feature's stability and known limitations transparently documented in a public support matrix. Built with native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose using Material 3 and dynamic colors, it leverages Android's Storage Access Framework for file access, runs longer jobs in a foreground service, and integrates native engines including FFmpeg, NCNN with Vulkan GPU acceleration, and bundled Google woff2. The app is aimed at Android users who want capable conversion tools without compromising their privacy or dealing with cluttered, ad-supported alternatives.

> Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform that provides a Firebase-like developer experience for building web, mobile, and AI applications. It combines enterprise-grade tools—including a hosted PostgreSQL database, PostgREST for auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, GoTrue for JWT-based authentication, realtime websocket subscriptions, S3-compatible file storage, edge functions, and a vector/embeddings toolkit for AI workloads. The platform is aimed at developers seeking a scalable, relational backend without vendor lock-in, leveraging Postgres as its foundation. Community support is provided through GitHub Discussions, Discord, and dedicated issue tracking, while an intuitive dashboard simplifies database management and configuration.

**Product Description Text**:
> AutoMQ is a cloud-first alternative to Kafka by decoupling durability to S3 and EBS. 10x cost-effective. Autoscale in seconds. Single-digit ms latency.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> AutoMQ is a cloud-native, diskless Kafka-compatible streaming platform designed to dramatically reduce the operational overhead and cost of running Apache Kafka by separating storage from compute and offloading data to S3-compatible object storage. By eliminating local disks and avoiding cross-AZ network traffic, it delivers up to 10x cost savings, second-level autoscaling, single-digit millisecond p99 latency, and multi-AZ high availability without the traditional replica traffic overhead. Its stateless architecture allows broker processes to be spun up or torn down on demand, enabling true elasticity for bursty workloads and pay-as-you-go consumption. AutoMQ is fully compatible with the Kafka protocol, so existing Kafka clients, tools, and applications work without modification, making migration straightforward. It is adopted in production by companies such as Grab, Tencent, LG U+, Honda, JD, miHoYo, and Geely for use cases including real-time analytics, log pipelines, gaming telemetry, and large-scale event streaming. The codebase is written primarily in Java and deploys via Docker Compose for evaluation or as a managed service on AWS, Tencent Cloud, and other cloud providers.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Postgres.js is the fastest full-featured PostgreSQL client for Node.js, Deno, Bun, and CloudFlare Workers, designed to deliver high performance with a minimal API surface. It uses ES6 tagged template strings as its core mechanism, enabling safe parameter interpolation that automatically prevents SQL injection while supporting dynamic query building for inserts, updates, and conditional fragments. The library offers comprehensive features including connection pooling, transactions, prepared statements, custom type transformations, LISTEN/NOTIFY, real-time subscriptions, and full TypeScript support. Connection is simple via a connection string, options object, or `psql` environment variables, and queries return arrays of result objects mapped by column name. Developers building JavaScript or TypeScript applications that require efficient, type-safe database access will benefit from its automatic value serialization, bigint and numeric handling, and ability to dynamically construct queries from objects or arrays.

Originally developed for internal use at Cloudflare, it solves the challenge of giving non-technical employees safe, company-context-aware AI tooling without overwhelming the security team. Its key features include an agent chat interface preloaded with company knowledge, sandboxed per-user application development where every user runs their own private instance of each app, and a capability-based security framework called "Gatekeepers" that wraps external services with OAuth authorization, narrow resource scoping, and an asynchronous human-in-the-loop approval system that simulates actions locally so agents can continue working. The technology stack centers on Cloudflare Workers, wrangler, and workerd for local development, with Gadgets running in isolated sandboxes and Gatekeepers implemented as separate Workers, making the architecture analogous to a traditional operating system where Gadgets act as processes and Gatekeepers serve as device drivers. The platform targets organizations that want to deploy customizable, AI-augmented productivity tools internally — with the explicit goal that adopters fork and rebrand it as their own "Company OS" rather than using Cloudflare's instance directly.

- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Github Awesome* | Video: *GitHub Trending Monthly #92026.07* | Published: *2026-08-01*
- **Attached Keywords**: `framework, typescript, tools, inference`

**Product Description Text**:
> scriptc is a TypeScript-to-native compiler that produces small, self-contained executables from ordinary TypeScript code without requiring Node, V8, or any embedded JavaScript engine by default. It addresses the long-standing gap between TypeScript's developer ergonomics and the deployment cost of shipping a full Node runtime, using a three-tier execution model: code is either compiled statically to native, runs through an embedded QuickJS engine when `--dynamic` is opted into for `any`-typed code and npm dependencies, or fails the build with a specific diagnostic—nothing is silently miscompiled. The compiler leverages TypeScript's own type checker and frontend via the tsc API, lowers to a typed IR, and emits either LLVM or C (via clang), with a vendored C runtime that provides refcounted values, a cycle collector, stackful fibers for async/await, a dependency-free event loop (kqueue), and the server stack (net, http, https, tls with mbedTLS, dns, fetch with WHATWG streams). Key features include differential testing against Node on an 800+ program corpus with byte-exact output comparison, AddressSanitizer + reference-count auditing on every change, escape hatches like `comptime()` for build-time evaluation and a Native FFI for C ABI calls, and binary sizes of 170–200KB statically with ~2.4ms startup. It's aimed at TypeScript developers building CLIs, servers, proxies, and edge functions who want Node's behavior with native performance, minimal footprint, and end-to-end safety

Nodes embed V8, execute Wrangler bundles, and coordinate entirely through the shared bucket, allowing applications to shard by construction while idle cells hibernate to near-zero resource usage. It targets developers who want the Durable Objects programming model without vendor lock-in, particularly teams building stateful edge or distributed applications on their own hardware. The stack is Rust-based with an embedded V8 runtime, integrates with standard AWS credentials, supports Wrangler-style deployments via esbuild, and includes operational tooling like `celld diagnose` plus pressure-based cell shedding.

**Product Description Text**:
> Cloudflare Computer is a virtual filesystem and pluggable execution environment built on Cloudflare's Durable Objects, providing a single workspace abstraction backed by authoritative SQLite state. The workspace exposes one execution entry point (`workspace.runtime.exec`) that can route to multiple interchangeable backends: a Container backend with full Linux userland via a FUSE mount and `computerd` daemon, a just-bash shell running in a Dynamic Worker, or an ECMAScript module evaluator with durable imports and `node:fs/promises` support. This lets developers choose between heavyweight sandbox execution and lightweight isolated runtimes against the same persistent filesystem, with backends connecting lazily and registering under stable IDs. The monorepo ships `@cloudflare/dofs` for the SQLite-backed VFS and sync protocol, `@cloudflare/computer-rpc` for capnweb wire types, the `computerd` daemon, and the top-level `@cloudflare/computer` package, alongside runnable examples including a chat agent, an artifacts publisher, and a tutorial that renders markdown to PDF. Performance benchmarks show the FUSE mount outperforms real disk on metadata-heavy workloads while trailing on large sequential I/O. The package is marked PREVIEW with unstable APIs, targeted at developers prototyping stateful agents, file-processing tools, and sandboxed code execution on Cloudflare's edge.

Key features include full OCI image support (pull, build, commit, push), a deny-by-default seccomp allowlist, cgroup v2 limits, and a `--security-profile untrusted` flag that bundles hardening for untrusted code; resource profiles for CPU, memory, disk, and devices declared once in `kern.toml` and reusable across both sandboxed boxes and host processes; compatibility with existing `docker-compose.yml` files via `kern compose`; and a Python/Node binding plus an MCP server for integrating with LangChain, Claude Desktop, or Cursor. Its dependency tree is intentionally minimal—just `libc`—with JSON and OCI parsing done by hand and image pulls delegated to the host's `curl` and `tar`. **Product Description Text**:
> generating videos, OmniRoute for routing AI provider requests with auto-fallback, and CapRover for self-hosted app deployment without manual Docker setup

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> MoneyPrinterTurbo is an open-source AI-powered short video generator that automates the entire video creation pipeline from a single topic or keyword. It leverages large language models (such as Kimi K3, DeepSeek, Doubao, and GPT) to write video scripts, extract search keywords for relevant footage, generate subtitles, and select background music, before synthesizing everything into a high-definition short video. The tool provides both a WebUI and an API interface, making it accessible to non-technical users while remaining flexible for developers, and it supports batch video generation as well as integration with various multimodal AI services for image, audio, and video generation. The fully automated workflow makes it well suited for content creators, social media marketers, and educators who need to produce short-form video content at scale without manual editing. Built primarily in Python and packaged with cross-platform support, it lowers the barrier to AI-driven video production by eliminating the need to stitch together multiple tools or possess video editing expertise.


#### 2. [vaultwarden](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden) (`dani-garcia/vaultwarden`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden)
- **Primary Language**: `Rust` | **Stars**: `★ 62,987` | **License**: `AGPL-3.0`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *ig_scraper* | Video: *IG Scraper Links* | Published: *2026-09-23*
- **Attached Keywords**: `security, rust, docker, self-hosted, framework`

**Product Description Text**:
> Vaultwarden, lightweight self-hosted password manager server. Vaultwarden is an open-source password manager server compatible with Bitwarden clients

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Vaultwarden is an unofficial, lightweight alternative server implementation of the Bitwarden Client API, written in Rust using the Rocket web framework. It enables self-hosted password management for users who want to run their own Bitwarden-compatible service without the resource demands of the official offering, while remaining fully compatible with official Bitwarden clients across desktop, mobile, and browser. The software provides a nearly complete implementation of the Bitwarden API, including personal vaults, organizations, collections, password sharing, directory connector, multi-factor authentication (Authenticator, Email, FIDO2/WebAuthn, YubiKey, Duo), emergency access, event logs, and an included modified Web Vault client. Deployment is streamlined through container images published to ghcr.io, Docker Hub, and Quay.io, with community-driven packages and source builds also available, typically behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS. Licensed under AGPL-3.0, the project is ideal for individuals, families, and organizations seeking full control over their credential storage infrastructure at minimal operational cost.


#### 3. [traefik](https://github.com/traefik/traefik) (`traefik/traefik`)

- **Attached Keywords**: `devops, networking, programming-languages, kubernetes, backend, cloud-computing`

**Product Description Text**:
> The Cloud Native Application Proxy

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Traefik is a modern HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer designed to simplify deploying microservices in cloud-native environments. It automatically integrates with orchestrators like Kubernetes, Docker, and Consul to dynamically configure routing based on service discovery. This eliminates the need for manual configuration of routes, which is often tedious in rapidly changing microservice deployments. Traefik ensures services are accessible via a single entry point while handling complex load balancing and traffic management. It natively supports HTTPS via Let's Encrypt and includes features like circuit breakers, metrics, and a web UI. As a Go-based binary, Traefik provides a fast, robust, and highly extensible solution for managing service traffic.

**Product Description Text**:
> Python SDK, Proxy Server (LLM Gateway) to call 100+ LLM APIs in OpenAI format - [Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI, VertexAI, Cohere, Anthropic, Sagemaker, HuggingFace, Replicate, Groq]

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> LiteLLM is an open-source AI Gateway that provides a single, unified interface to call 100+ large language model providers—including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, and vLLM—using the standard OpenAI format. It eliminates the friction of juggling provider-specific SDKs, authentication patterns, and request formats by offering both a Python SDK for direct library integration and a self-hosted Proxy Server for centralized team or enterprise use. Key features include drop-in OpenAI compatibility, virtual keys, cost and spend tracking, guardrails, load balancing, request logging, and an admin dashboard, all delivered with a Rust core for high performance (8ms P95 latency at 1k RPS). The platform also supports A2A agent invocation across frameworks like LangGraph and Azure AI Foundry, as well as endpoints for embeddings, images, audio, and reranking. It is designed for developers, ML engineers, and organizations that need production-ready, multi-provider LLM orchestration without rewriting code when swapping models. Notable adopters include Stripe, Google ADK, Greptile, OpenHands, Netflix, and the OpenAI Agents SDK.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> FlClash is an open-source, ad-free multi-platform proxy client built on ClashMeta, designed to provide a simple and user-friendly way to manage network proxy connections across Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. It addresses the need for a unified, cross-device proxy solution by supporting subscription links, multiple color themes, dark mode, and data synchronization via WebDAV, all wrapped in a Material You design inspired by Surfboard's UI. The app is ideal for users seeking privacy, bypassing geo-restrictions, or managing complex proxy configurations without platform-specific tooling. Built using Flutter for the frontend and Golang for the proxy core, it leverages native platform integrations and offers installation via F-Droid, GitHub releases, and Homebrew. Developers can build it across platforms using provided Dart setup scripts, with platform-specific dependencies like Android NDK, GCC, or Inno Setup as needed.

**Product Description Text**:
> Xray panel supporting multi-protocol multi-user expire day & traffic & ip limit (Vmess & Vless & Trojan & ShadowSocks & Wireguard)

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> 3X-UI is an open-source web-based control panel for managing Xray-core proxy and VPN servers, providing a centralized interface to deploy, configure, and monitor multi-protocol network setups across single VPS or multi-node environments. As an enhanced fork of the original X-UI, it supports a wide range of protocols including VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, WireGuard, Hysteria2, and more, with modern transports (WebSocket, gRPC, XHTTP) and security options (TLS, XTLS, REALITY). The panel offers granular per-client management with traffic quotas, expiry dates, IP limits, and live status monitoring, alongside built-in subscription services, Telegram bot integration, and a RESTful API with Swagger documentation. It is built in Go, supports both SQLite and PostgreSQL backends, and ships with a multilingual UI (13 languages) featuring dark and light themes. Designed for individual administrators and small-to-medium hosting providers, it includes unattended installation scripts, Docker support, Fail2ban integration, and broad compatibility across Linux distributions and CPU architectures.

**Product Description Text**:
> ⚠️ Browser fingerprinting via favicon!

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supercookie demonstrates a browser fingerprinting technique that exploits the favicon cache (F-Cache) to assign persistent, unique identifiers to website visitors. By serving favicons from a combinatorial set of URL paths and observing which requests are made versus served from cache, a server can reconstruct a binary pattern that identifies a browser with 100% accuracy. Unlike conventional cookies, this tracking method survives cache flushing, browser restarts, VPN usage, incognito/private mode, and even certain anti-tracking service workers, making it a significant privacy concern. The repository includes a fully functional web server (deployable via Docker or Node.js) that performs the favicon-based tracking, along with a live demo and comprehensive documentation explaining the threat model. Inspired by academic research from the University of Illinois, Chicago, it serves as an educational tool to raise awareness of this stealth tracking vector affecting all major desktop and mobile browsers. The technology stack is lightweight, relying on a Node.js backend with a configurable environment for hosting the tracking infrastructure.

> ymawky is a minimalist, single-purpose web server written entirely in hand-crafted ARM64 assembly language for macOS (with a Linux branch available), using direct syscalls without any libc dependency. It addresses the niche need for a deeply transparent, educational web server that demonstrates low-level systems programming on Apple Silicon, appealing to developers interested in assembly, networking fundamentals, or unconventional server implementations. Key features include a fork-per-connection model, support for HTTP methods (GET, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, HEAD, and POST via CGI), MIME type detection, Range requests for video scrubbing, atomic file uploads via temporary files, hex-decoded URL paths, and path traversal protection with `O_NOFOLLOW_ANY`. It also offers experimental CGI script execution within a confined `cgi-bin/` directory, configurable via a `config.S` file, along with built-in slowloris mitigation through 10-second timeouts. The server serves static files from a `www/` document root with customizable error pages, runs on `127.0.0.1` by default, and is built simply using `make` with Xcode Command Line Tools.

**Product Description Text**:
> *(No brief description text provided in original record)*

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> OpenFlux is a network stack research tool that establishes a TCP tunnel over pluggable transports, enabling packet-level traffic forwarding through a client and exit-node architecture. It targets developers and researchers experimenting with network tunneling, transport obfuscation, and exit-node design, and ships clients for macOS (utun L3), Linux, Windows, Android, and iOS (NEPacketTunnelProvider). The exit node supports two backends selected via `--mode`: `l3`, a raw SNAT/DNAT forwarder using SOCK_RAW and conntrack on Linux with root, and `l4`, a userspace gVisor-based TCP proxy (`proxy` is a deprecated alias) that works on any platform without privileges. Transports include Yandex.Docs (WebSocket), Yandex Volga, MAX/OneMe (WebRTC DataChannel), Cups.online (Centrifugo rooms), and Mail.ru Docs, all wrapped by a batched zstd codec (`transport/batched.go`) that coalesces tunnel packets to reduce message overhead and improve throughput, with optional AES-256-GCM encryption via a shared key. The client terminates TCP locally through gVisor, utun, or NEPacketTunnelProvider and sends raw IP packets into the transport, yielding an end-to-end single TCP connection in `l3` mode and double-termination in `l4` mode. The codebase is written in Go (with platform-specific cgo for iOS) and is provided as a non-commercial, as-is research artifact.

#### 77. [tailcat](https://github.com/tailscale/tailcat) (`tailscale/tailcat`)

- **Attached Keywords**: `security, cli, proxy, go`

**Product Description Text**:
> Tailcat. A Netcat-style tunnel through a Tailscale network

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Tailcat is a netcat-like command-line tool and Go library that leverages Tailscale's open-source data plane (magicsock) to provide encrypted, peer-to-peer tunnels without requiring Tailscale's control plane or an account. It solves the problem of securely connecting two machines through NAT-traversed WireGuard tunnels using out-of-band token exchange, making it ideal for ad-hoc file transfers, remote shells, port forwarding, and SOCKS5 proxying without modifying system routing tables or DNS. Key features include stdin/stdout piping, TCP port exposure, an auth-free SSH server, SFTP-based file serving (using Go's `os.Root` for path confinement), NAT hole-punching via DERP relays with automatic upgrade to direct UDP connections, and an experimental WebAssembly browser demo. The tool runs entirely in userspace with no root/admin privileges needed, supports multiple installation methods (Homebrew, Nix, AUR, Docker, static binaries), and can use either Tailscale's rate-limited DERP relays or self-hosted ones. Built in Go, it is designed for developers, sysadmins, and privacy-conscious users who need simple, ephemeral, end-to-end encrypted point-to-point communication.

It supports custom subdomains, configurable schemes (HTTP/HTTPS), and host/port forwarding, while providing an introspection dashboard for monitoring traffic. The client is easy to install via Homebrew, Cargo, or pre-built binaries, and a simple `tunnelto --port 8000` command is enough to tunnel localhost traffic. The server component can be self-hosted, with configuration via environment variables detailed in the source, though self-hosted deployments lack centralized coordination across multiple server instances. The hosted version at tunnelto.dev runs as a distributed system on fly.io, leveraging its Private Networking feature with a gossip mechanism for coordination. Built entirely on async-io with tokio, tunnelto is well-suited for web developers, QA testers, and anyone needing quick public access to local services.

It addresses the need for granular, audited access management in DMZ environments by allowing administrators to assign specific users to specific internal hosts and URLs, then forwarding connections straight to targets. Key capabilities include full session recording with live viewing and replay through an admin web UI, browser-based SSH/RDP/VNC access, native two-factor authentication, OpenID Connect SSO, and built-in brute-force protection with IP blocking. Designed for sysadmins, DevOps teams, and security-conscious organizations seeking self-hosted alternatives to VPNs or tools like Teleport, it supports both interactive and non-interactive connections while storing audit data in SQLite. Implemented as a single dependency-free binary in 100% safe Rust, with a Svelte-based admin UI, Warpgate is actively used in enterprise settings and distributes official builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

It utilizes Channel State Information (CSI) captured by low-cost ESP32 sensors to detect human presence, activity, and vital signs without requiring any cameras or wearables. Ultimately, RuView provides a camera-free, low-power solution for presence detection and health monitoring.

- **Attached Keywords**: `postgresql, python, workflow, orchestration`
- **GitHub Topics**: `dbos, durable, temporal, workflow`

**Product Description Text**:
> DBOSify is a drop-in replacement for Temporal Python that uses Postgres—via the DBOS Transact library—as its workflow orchestration backend, eliminating the need for a separate Temporal server. It enables developers to run durable workflows, activities, signals, updates, retries, and recovery using only a Postgres database as infrastructure. At its core, a deterministic interpreter executes each workflow coroutine and its signal, update, and query handlers on a virtual event loop that advances only when events arrive, checkpointing all nondeterministic actions in Postgres before the workflow observes them. Activities and timers become DBOS steps and durable sleeps; signals, updates, and cancellations are delivered through Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY; and namespaces map to distinct Postgres schemas. The library is aimed at Python developers building reliable, long-running applications who want Temporal's durable execution semantics without the operational overhead of running a Temporal cluster. It is tested through ported Temporal unit and integration tests, sample applications, kill-and-recover scenarios, and signature-parity checks, though it is not wire-compatible with other Temporal SDKs and lacks the Temporal Web UI or CLI tooling.

> **effect-mq** — Effect-native background job processing for TypeScript

A schema-first job queue built on [Effect](https://effect.website) v4 that brings the proven semantics of BullMQ — retries, repeatable schedules, deduplication, and worker runtimes — into Effect's typed, structured-concurrency world. Jobs are defined as class schemas with payloads, success types, idempotency keys, and retry defaults baked in, eliminating string-based handler lookup and untyped payloads.

The package splits into tree-shakeable modules: `effect-mq` for the storage-agnostic core, `drizzle-postgres` for a Drizzle-native Postgres store with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claims, `redis` for an atomic-Lua Redis backend, and `testing` for conformance drivers. Every attempt is persisted in a run ledger, dedup, throttle, debounce, and cross-process cancellation work with Effect fibers, and metrics integrate with the Effect `Metric` system. Drizzle-kit owns migrations because the job tables are plain schema factories users re-export.

Teams already running Effect services that need durable, observable background work — email sends, image processing, scheduled data pipelines — get compile-time wiring of stores to jobs, runtime safety from `Schema.Redacted`, and the same control primitives (`timeout`, `interrupt`, `pause`) they use elsewhere in their app.

> OpenArchiver is a self-hosted, open-source email archiving platform that enables organizations to maintain permanent, tamper-proof records of their communications without vendor lock-in. It solves the problem of email preservation and compliance by supporting ingestion from Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, generic IMAP servers, PST files, and .eml/mbox archives, with both bulk imports and continuous real-time synchronization. Archived emails are stored in standard .eml format with deduplication, compression, at-rest encryption, and cryptographic hashing, and each email includes an Integrity Report to verify authenticity. The platform offers full-text search across emails and attachments, threaded conversation discovery, granular retention policies, legal holds, and an immutable audit trail for regulatory compliance. It targets IT administrators, compliance officers, and organizations needing eDiscovery capabilities, particularly those handling regulated data or operating in jurisdictions with strict record-keeping requirements. The stack combines SvelteKit on the frontend, Node.js/Express/TypeScript on the backend, BullMQ on Redis/Valkey for job processing, Meilisearch for search, and PostgreSQL for metadata, all deployed via Docker Compose with pluggable local or S3-compatible storage backends.

**Product Description Text**:
> backup-maker is a self-hosted backup tool that automatically mirrors chosen folders to multiple local destinations in real time, including USB drives, NAS shares, router-attached storage, SD cards, and folders on other computers on the same network. It is installed only on the machine being protected, with no software, accounts, or configuration required on destination devices—shared folders and NAS boxes are reached via a built-in SMB client that needs no mounting or admin rights. Backups run as continuous incremental copies that keep roughly 30 days of previous file versions, while a separate timed mode produces AES-256 encrypted zip snapshots on a schedule for sealed, point-in-time recovery. The project is written in Go and ships as a single self-contained binary per OS for Linux, Windows, and macOS, with both a CLI and a localhost-only web dashboard for setup and monitoring. Privacy is enforced by design: no cloud, no telemetry, no public discovery, with network scanning, update checks, and webhook/ntfy alerts all disabled by default. It targets home users and small offices who want straightforward, local, versioned backups without third-party services, and optionally supports a second paired machine for block-level delta syncing using a vendored, checksum-verified Syncthing build.

**Product Description Text**:
> *(No brief description text provided in original record)*

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> restoredrill is a CI-native verification tool that proves PostgreSQL and MySQL backups actually restore, not just that backup jobs succeeded. It fetches the latest backup, restores it into a throwaway container, runs tiered checks (file freshness/RPO, structural integrity, row counts and custom SQL assertions, RTO timing, and environment sanity), and emits a JSON report with timestamped, auditor-friendly fields rather than relying on logs or self-attested policy documents. Every check fails closed, invalid configurations are rejected at load time, and notification delivery failures surface as findings so an audit cannot quietly skip a broken run. An `existing_connection` mode skips restore tiers for environments that already maintain a fresh copy, running the same read-path checks instead. The tool targets engineering and compliance teams pursuing SOC 2, ISO 27001, or AWS Foundational Technical Review who need reproducible evidence with stable schema fields in `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC"` format that survive copying into spreadsheets. Built in Go with a YAML configuration, it operates as a scheduled CLI job rather than a continuously running daemon, fitting cleanly into existing backup pipelines without production credentials.

> Rejourney is an open-source, self-hostable or hosted observability tool for web and mobile apps, focused on being lightweight and performant. It provides traces, errors, and performance metrics without the overhead of full APM suites. The platform is aimed at developers and small teams who want simple observability without enterprise pricing. Rejourney is positioned as a streamlined alternative to heavy APM tools.


#### 22. [awesome-open-saas](https://github.com/nikhilrayaprolu/awesome-open-saas) (`nikhilrayaprolu/awesome-open-saas`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/nikhilrayaprolu/awesome-open-saas](https://github.com/nikhilrayaprolu/awesome-open-saas)
- **Primary Language**: `Not specified` | **Stars**: `★ 242` | **License**: `MIT`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Cooly* | Video: *Cooly's Chrome Links* | Published: *2026-09-02*
- **Attached Keywords**: `awesome-list, productivity, self-hosted, developer-tools, tools, open-source, alternatives`

**Product Description Text**:
> A Curated List of Open Source Software as a Service Products

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> awesome-open-saas is a curated list of open-source alternatives to popular proprietary Software as a Service (SaaS) products. It addresses the lack of awareness around open-source SaaS options by mapping well-known commercial tools to their community-driven counterparts, making it easy for developers and businesses to discover self-hostable alternatives. The repository covers categories including cloud storage, error tracking, project management, authentication, search, communication, and CMS, featuring products like Supabase, Sentry, GitLab, Hoppscotch, and Zulip. Each entry includes the open-source product name, deployment type (hosted, manual, or library), and the programming languages used. It also welcomes community contributions, allowing new open SaaS projects to be listed once they receive sufficient support through GitHub issues.
