- **GitHub Topics**: `generative-art, non-photorealistic-rendering, npr, pen-plotter, rendering, sketch, svg, typescript`

**Product Description Text**:
> Krbn is a browser-based TypeScript engine that renders 3D scenes as non-photorealistic, pencil-style SVG illustrations instead of pixel-based images. Rather than computing per-pixel color like traditional rasterizers, it derives and styles strokes directly from geometry: sphere and cone silhouettes emerge as exact conics, torus outlines as exact quartics, and hidden lines are split analytically into visible and ghosted runs rather than z-buffered away. The pipeline supports analytic primitives (spheres, cylinders, cones, planes, ellipsoids, tori), free-form curves (Béziers, helices, function plots), and arbitrary triangle meshes, all routed through a shared five-stage pass that produces silhouettes, hidden-line occlusion, curvature-following hatching, suggestive contours, creases, and intersection seams. Shading is expressed as cross-hatch density, with stroke direction flowing along each surface's own curvature field, and transparency is implicit in the gaps between strokes the way it is on paper. Output is deterministic across renders on a given platform, producing byte-identical, diffable SVG, and an animated camera orbit stays visually stable because wobble is keyed to stroke identity rather than recomputed per frame. Developers, technical illustrators, educators, and researchers producing math, physics, or technical diagrams will find it useful, and the project is MIT-licensed with a roadmap targeting medical and organic illustration.

> OpticalModeler is an evidence-gated Agent Skill that converts 2D photonics schematics into physically auditable 3D optical tables inside Blender. It treats optical topology, real apertures, manufacturer CAD, fasteners, load paths, fiber routing, and artifact lineage as strict acceptance gates rather than decorative details, producing fail-closed evidence through reopened-scene audits, ray/BVH checks, hashes, manifests, and explicit PASS/BLOCKED/UNVERIFIED states. The target users are photonics researchers, optical engineers, and laboratory staff who need trustworthy, reproducible reconstructions of complex optical setups for documentation, review, or planning purposes. The technology stack centers on Blender for 3D rendering and physics simulation, STEP/CAD asset integration, ray tracing with BVH acceleration, and an Agent Skills framework (installable via `npx skills add`) that guides autonomous agents through a six-stage reconstruction and audit pipeline. Released under the MIT License, it serves as an independent community tool with a sanitized G1/G2 case study demonstrating end-to-end workflow from schematic input to verified 3D output.

**Product Description Text**:
> Proto Language is an open-source Python framework for designing biological sequences—DNA, RNA, and proteins—through constraint-based generative optimization. Users specify a design as a set of constraints, and the framework executes a propose–score–refine loop to search for sequences that satisfy them, leveraging a large suite of computational biology and AI tools (structure predictors, protein language models, inverse folding, aligners, and gene annotation) to score candidates. The system is built around seven core primitives—`Sequence`, `Segment`, `Construct`, `Constraint`, `Generator`, `Optimizer`, and `Program`—each with a Pydantic-based configuration pattern, allowing extensible registration of new tools via decorators. It targets computational biologists, protein engineers, and bioinformaticians who need to express complex design pipelines without low-level orchestration, and supports both local and hosted execution through the accompanying `proto-client` SDK. Backed by the `proto-tools` execution layer, every computationally intensive tool runs in its own automatically provisioned, isolated environment, eliminating manual dependency management. The package is MIT-licensed, requires Python 3.10+, and integrates with gated models such as ESM3, AlphaGenome, and AlphaFold3 via HuggingFace authentication.

> *(No brief description text provided in original record)*

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> ABot-Recon addresses long-horizon streaming 3D reconstruction from video by deliberately avoiding persistent long-range memory, instead reconstructing global geometry from a fixed 12-frame local context through per-frame point map prediction and adjacent relative pose estimation. The model composes local poses sequentially to recover the full trajectory, keeping both model-state memory and per-frame computation independent of sequence length, while a motion-visual rotation refiner and composition-aware pose loss mitigate accumulated drift. It achieves strong results on benchmarks such as Oxford Spires (ATE 4.35 m, F1 91.81%) and KITTI (24.45 FPS at 6.71 GiB on an H100), and an optional loop-closure backend using DINOv2-SALAD retrieval and pose-graph optimization can be enabled when sequences contain revisits. Researchers and engineers working on online 3D mapping, SLAM, AR/VR scene capture, or long-video geometric understanding will find it useful, particularly given its edge deployment story (Axera AX650N NPU port) and interactive Hugging Face demo. The stack is Python 3.10+ with PyTorch 2.5.1 and CUDA 12.1, optionally accelerated by FlashInfer paged KV-cache operators and a compiled cuRoPE extension.

This design eliminates common UV-mapping artifacts such as seams, distortion, wasted atlas space, duplicated vertices, and uneven texel resolution. The system supports surface-aware optimization with importance pruning and error-based densification, and can be fitted from existing textured meshes or from multi-view image observations while remaining differentiable and compatible with physically based rendering via Mitsuba 3.7.1. Released as the implementation of the ECCV 2026 Best Paper by Foti, Korkmaz, Zafeiriou, and Birdal, the codebase targets researchers and practitioners in 3D vision, geometry processing, and neural rendering who need high-quality textures on arbitrary mesh topology. The technology stack centers on PyTorch 2.10 with CUDA 12.9, torch-geometric, custom geodesic KNN heat-kernel routines, and supporting libraries including libigl, trimesh, point-cloud-utils, robust_laplacian, and potpourri3d, with an optional environment for tiny-cuda-nn-based neural texture baselines.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> PaperGym addresses the challenge of generating high-quality research plans with LLMs by introducing a rubric-centered training framework that converts academic papers into low-leakage training environments. Its pipeline first extracts rubrics from arXiv papers to synthesize 20,000 instances across five domains (PaperGym-20k), then applies a two-stage "teach-explore" paradigm: rubric-conditioned self-distillation (OPSD) followed by GRPO with rubric-as-reward, using the extracted rubrics twice to improve both supervision and reinforcement signals. The approach achieves only 3.7% criterion leakage (3–9× lower than existing benchmarks), delivers +4.8 to +5.6 point gains over base Qwen3 models, and reaches a 58.1% win rate against baselines while surpassing the much larger Kimi K2.6 on ResearchQA with a fine-tuned 8B model. Researchers working on automated scientific reasoning, LLM post-training, or rubric-based evaluation will find the released corpus, fine-tuned models (1B/4B/8B), and held-out benchmarks (PaperGym-Innov, PaperGym-Design) directly useful. The codebase is built on PyTorch with TRL for the OPSD stage, verl for GRPO, vLLM for inference, and includes comprehensive evaluation tooling for leakage detection, win-rate comparisons, entropy analysis, and scorer stability.

The library includes format-agnostic `DataReader`/`DataWriter` abstractions, trivia-preserving JSON5 editing, and compatibility shims for System.Text.Json, Newtonsoft.Json, and DataContractJsonSerializer, all under an Apache-2.0 license. It is developed as a core component of CAPCOM's "REX" next-generation game engine technology. #### 1. [open-webui](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) (`open-webui/open-webui`)

**Product Description Text**:
> User-friendly WebUI for LLMs (Formerly Ollama WebUI)

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Open WebUI is a self-hosted, offline-capable AI platform that provides a user-friendly interface for interacting with large language models, addressing the need for a private, extensible alternative to cloud-based AI chat services. It supports multiple LLM runners including Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API (such as LMStudio, GroqCloud, and vLLM), enabling users to mix local and remote inference providers seamlessly. Key features include built-in Retrieval Augmented Generation with support for nine vector databases, granular role-based access control, a robust plugin system with MCP integration, and collaborative tools like shared Channels, persistent memory, and AI-assisted scheduling. It offers a responsive Progressive Web App with full Markdown/LaTeX rendering, voice and video calling capabilities, image generation, multi-model conversations, and enterprise-ready features such as LDAP/SSO/SCIM authentication, OpenTelemetry observability, and horizontal scalability via Redis. Ideal for developers, IT administrators, research teams, and enterprises seeking a customizable, secure AI deployment, Open WebUI is built with a modern technology stack including Python (backend), Svelte/TypeScript (frontend), Docker/Kubernetes support, and flexible database options (SQLite or PostgreSQL).

**Product Description Text**:
> Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Storybook is an open-source frontend workshop that enables developers to build, document, and test UI components in isolation, separate from the main application. It solves the challenge of developing and validating components without needing to navigate through full app states, making UI development faster and more reliable. The tool supports a wide range of frameworks including React, Angular, Vue, Svelte, Preact, Ember, SolidJS, Qwik, HTML, and Web Components, with extensions for React Native, Android, iOS, and Flutter. It features a rich ecosystem of addons for component design, documentation, testing, and interactivity, with an extensible API for custom configurations. Trusted by thousands of teams, Storybook serves frontend developers, design system maintainers, and QA engineers seeking to create bulletproof, reusable UI components. Continuous integration is ensured through CircleCI builds and Codecov coverage, while an active community provides support via Discord and GitHub Discussions.

**Product Description Text**:
> Huly — All-in-One Project Management Platform (alternative to Linear, Jira, Slack, Notion, Motion)

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Huly Platform is an open-source, all-in-one project management framework that serves as an alternative to tools like Linear, Jira, Slack, Notion, and Motion, consolidating multiple business workflows into a single system. It bundles several built-in apps—including Chat, Project Management, CRM, HRM, and an Applicant Tracking System (ATS)—and also functions as a foundation for teams to build custom business applications. The framework is used in production by products such as Huly and TraceX, making it suitable for startups, enterprises, and developers seeking a customizable, self-hosted productivity suite. Developers interact with the platform through a typed API client for building integrations and custom extensions. The technology stack is TypeScript- and Svelte-based, using Rush as a monorepo orchestrator, with Docker and Docker Compose for containerized deployment across Linux and macOS (amd64 and arm64). Note that while self-hosted deployments remain supported, the hosted Huly service is being discontinued, requiring users to migrate their data before July 20.

**Product Description Text**:
> The AI Toolkit for TypeScript. From the creators of Next.js, the AI SDK is a free open-source library for building AI-powered applications and agents

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> The AI SDK is a free, open-source TypeScript toolkit designed for building AI-powered applications and agents. It provides a provider-agnostic, unified API for interacting with various large language models, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, typically leveraging the Vercel AI Gateway. This architecture allows developers to seamlessly switch between model providers while maintaining a consistent development experience. The SDK enables developers to easily generate text and structured data using these models. Furthermore, it includes tools for building complex AI agents, such as the `ToolLoopAgent`, which can interact with external tools. The SDK also offers framework-agnostic UI modules to simplify the integration of generative user interfaces across popular frameworks like Next.js, React, and Svelte.

**Product Description Text**:
> OpenUI let's you describe UI using your imagination, then see it rendered live.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> OpenUI is an open-source tool for rapidly creating and iterating on user interfaces with natural-language prompts and live rendering. It helps developers and designers turn imaginative UI ideas into working components without manually writing the initial implementation, then request targeted changes through conversational instructions. Generated HTML can be converted into frameworks and formats such as React, Svelte, and Web Components, making it useful for prototyping and exploring LLM-powered application tooling. The platform supports models from OpenAI, Groq, Google, Anthropic, Cohere, Mistral, LiteLLM-compatible providers, and local Ollama models. It can be run locally with Python and uv, through Docker, or accessed through a hosted live demo. OpenUI is developed as a Python backend with a modern JavaScript frontend and is used by Weights & Biases to test next-generation tools for building applications on top of large language models.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> phantom-ui is a structure-aware skeleton loader distributed as a single Web Component built with Lit, eliminating the need to author and maintain separate skeleton versions of UI components. It works by rendering the real component with transparent placeholder text, measuring every leaf element's position and size via `getBoundingClientRect`, and overlaying animated shimmer blocks at those exact coordinates while preserving container backgrounds and borders. Because it is a standards-based custom element, it integrates with React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Solid, Qwik, HTMX, and plain HTML without framework-specific adapters. Installation options include npm, bun, pnpm, yarn, a CDN script tag, or a vendored standalone ES module (34 kB minified, 11.5 kB gzipped) for projects without registry access or `node_modules`, with TypeScript declarations that type-check under strict mode with no configuration. An optional `init` command auto-generates JSX type declarations for React, Solid, and Qwik and adds pre-hydration CSS for SSR frameworks like Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix, and Qwik, while leaving the codebase untouched when skipped (no postinstall hook runs).

Users, the agent, and an automatic Conductor can collaboratively manage which blocks stay full, fold into summaries, or remain pinned, with the most recent ~20k tokens protected as a high-fidelity working tail. Its flagship Conductor, Thermocline, scores block relevance using a 500M-parameter attention model and demonstrated 83.3% accuracy on SlopCodeBench versus 33.3% for naive compaction at the same 100k-token budget. The stack includes a Tauri + SvelteKit desktop app for the Map view, a pi extension for agent integration, and reversible `{#code FOLDED}` digests that let the agent recall folded context as tool results without expanding it back into the working window.

It solves the problem of feeding documents to large language models efficiently, since sending pages as images to vision models is expensive and plain text extractors lose structure and fail on scanned PDFs, returning empty results. The app supports a wide range of formats including PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, EPUB, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, images, and audio, with built-in OCR that recovers text from scanned documents that other tools read as blank. It produces Markdown that uses 2 to 6 times fewer tokens than vision-model alternatives, preserving headings, tables, and lists while stripping layout noise. Key features include batch folder processing, optional cleanup passes (rule-based, local AI, or API), per-file diagnostics, and a portable setup that runs entirely offline after initial installation. Built on Microsoft's MarkItDown library, MDFlux targets AI/RAG builders, researchers, developers, and privacy-conscious users who need to convert sensitive or large document collections without uploading anything to the cloud.

It addresses the common pain point where standard chart libraries break down when visualizations need to extend beyond basic line or bar charts into product-specific designs, offering a single typed grammar that scales from simple to custom without requiring a parallel data model or API. **Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Morphicons is a zero-dependency library that morphs any stroke-based icon into any other with spring physics, supporting Lucide, Tabler, Heroicons, Iconoir, or custom path data. It solves the dual problems of naive coordinate interpolation (which shears shapes mid-transition) and the tedious requirement to hand-declare rotation groups for congruent icon pairs like arrow-right → arrow-down, instead computing optimal 2D shape alignment via closed-form Procrustes analysis so rotations emerge naturally from the math. The library exposes unified bindings for React, Vue, Svelte, React Native, plus framework-agnostic Web Component and Astro shells, all sharing an identical API with three usage modes: uncontrolled (just change the prop), controlled (bind to external progress), and imperative (ref-based `morphTo` / `set`). It consumes icon *data* (`IconNode` or raw `d` strings from the vanilla `lucide` package) rather than framework-specific components, making it a drop-in replacement for `lucide-react` with full prop pass-through (`size`, `strokeWidth`, `color`, `className`, etc.) and accessible defaults (`aria-hidden` unless labeled, `role="img"` + `<title>` otherwise). SSR is clean—the server emits static SVG with zero flash—and morphs play regardless of OS reduce-motion by default, with an opt-in `reducedMotion="user"` mode.

Designers and developers can use the companion visual editor at shaders.com to compose effects on an infinite canvas and export production-ready component code, while an accompanying CLI integrates those designs directly into codebases with framework detection and lock-file tracking. The library is also AI-friendly, offering an installable agent skill, an MCP server for tools like Claude Code and Cursor, and an llms.txt index for documentation retrieval. Trusted by over 16,000 design engineers, the core engine and components are free under an MIT license, with an optional Pro tier unlocking 1,000+ presets, full website sections, and HD rendering without watermarks.

> supabase-auth-doctor is a read-only CLI that diagnoses common Supabase Auth configuration mistakes in OAuth, PKCE, redirect URLs, environment variables, and Vercel deployments, surfacing issues that typically appear as generic provider or callback failures. It runs with a single `npx supabase-auth-doctor` command (Node.js 20+, zero runtime dependencies) and produces a PASS / WARN / FAIL / UNKNOWN report with actionable fixes rather than just a status code. The tool inspects local `.env` files for common Supabase URL and anon/secret key patterns across Next.js, Vite, Expo, and generic projects, scans application source (JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX/TSX, Vue, Svelte, Astro) for `signInWithOAuth`, `redirectTo`, and `exchangeCodeForSession` usage, and verifies Supabase Auth reachability plus the hosted provider callback URL at `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`. An optional, deeper check uses a scoped Management API token to compare local settings against dashboard Auth configuration, including Site URL and the redirect allow-list. Developers working with Supabase Auth on web frameworks, especially those deploying to Vercel, would use it to cut debugging time when OAuth flows break for unclear reasons. Support commands include `--provider <name>`, `--offline`, `--json`, and `explain` for a visual breakdown of the OAuth route.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Warpgate is a transparent bastion host that secures access to SSH, HTTPS, Kubernetes, MySQL, PostgreSQL, RDP, and VNC services without requiring custom clients or SSH wrappers. It addresses the need for granular, audited access management in DMZ environments by allowing administrators to assign specific users to specific internal hosts and URLs, then forwarding connections straight to targets. Key capabilities include full session recording with live viewing and replay through an admin web UI, browser-based SSH/RDP/VNC access, native two-factor authentication, OpenID Connect SSO, and built-in brute-force protection with IP blocking. Designed for sysadmins, DevOps teams, and security-conscious organizations seeking self-hosted alternatives to VPNs or tools like Teleport, it supports both interactive and non-interactive connections while storing audit data in SQLite. Implemented as a single dependency-free binary in 100% safe Rust, with a Svelte-based admin UI, Warpgate is actively used in enterprise settings and distributes official builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

**Product Description Text**:
> Use Livewire as the reactivity store and implement the frontend in any framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact, Lit, Alpine islands). GH: 0★, pushed 2026-10-06.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Wire Bridge enables React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact, Lit, and Alpine components to share and react to the same state as Blade inputs within a Livewire 4 page, without triggering HTTP requests on every edit. Livewire remains the canonical state owner; islands read cached `$wire` snapshots and write back through `$wire.$set`, so a React input, Vue's totals, and a Svelte delivery picker can all edit one Livewire component in real time. The library provides framework adapters (`useWireField` for Preact, React, and Vue; `createWireField` for Solid; a Svelte-compatible store; plus plain bindings for Lit and Alpine) and exposes a framework-agnostic core (`createWireBridge`) that only depends on Livewire's public browser API (`$get`, `$set`, `$watch`, `$commit`, `$call`). PHP is contacted only when calling `commit()` or `call()`, keeping the network round-trips minimal. It is distributed as ES modules with TypeScript declarations and zero runtime dependencies, targeting Laravel developers who need to embed third-party-framework islands inside Livewire 4 pages.

> Clash Verge Rev is a modern, cross-platform Graphical User Interface (GUI) client designed for managing Clash Meta configurations. Built using the Tauri framework, the application is developed in TypeScript and Rust, ensuring high performance and stability across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Key features include support for system proxy, TUN (virtual network card) mode, and visual editing of nodes and rules. The client offers a clean, customizable interface with support for various configuration management tools. Ultimately, Clash Verge Rev provides a tailored and powerful experience for advanced proxy users.

**Product Description Text**:
> Build smaller, faster, and more secure desktop and mobile applications with a web frontend.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Tauri enables developers to build small, fast, and secure desktop and mobile applications using familiar web front-end technologies. Its Rust-powered backend exposes APIs that the HTML, JavaScript, and CSS interface can call, combining web development flexibility with native application capabilities. The framework uses the operating system’s webview through WRY—WKWebView on macOS and iOS, WebView2 on Windows, WebKitGTK on Linux, and Android System WebView—while TAO manages application windows. It includes app bundling, desktop self-updates, system tray icons, native notifications, a secure native WebView protocol, CI tooling, and VS Code support. Tauri is ideal for web and Rust developers creating cross-platform applications for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS without shipping a large JavaScript runtime.

**Product Description Text**:
> TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> TradingAgents is a multi-agent LLM framework that simulates the structure of real-world trading firms to collaboratively evaluate market conditions and inform investment strategies. The platform deploys specialized agents across four teams: an Analyst Team (Fundamentals, Sentiment, News, and Technical analysts) that gathers and interprets diverse market data, a Researcher Team with bullish and bearish agents that debate the analysts' insights to weigh risk versus reward, a Trader Agent that synthesizes reports into actionable decisions, and a Risk Management/Portfolio Manager layer that evaluates volatility and liquidity before approving or rejecting trades for execution on a simulated exchange. Designed primarily for research purposes, the framework supports multiple LLM providers (including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints), integrates data vendors such as FRED and Polymarket, and offers features like structured-output agents, LangGraph checkpoint resume, backtesting, Docker deployment, and configurable environment variables. Researchers, quantitative analysts, and AI/fintech developers exploring multi-agent systems and automated trading strategies would find this framework particularly useful. The technology stack is Python-based, leveraging LangGraph for agent orchestration and supporting both cloud APIs and local model serving via Ollama.

**Product Description Text**:

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Voicebox is a local-first, open-source AI voice studio that unifies voice cloning, text-to-speech generation, and system-wide dictation into a single desktop application, positioning itself as a privacy-respecting alternative to cloud services like ElevenLabs and WisprFlow. It supports seven TTS engines—including Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox, Kokoro, and HumeAI TADA—covering 23 languages with capabilities ranging from zero-shot voice cloning and 50+ preset voices to paralinguistic emotion tags like `[laugh]` and `[sigh]`, plus post-processing effects such as pitch shift, reverb, and compression. A global hotkey enables push-to-talk or toggle dictation into any text field using Whisper-based STT, while a bundled local LLM powers compose, rewrite, and respond modes through configurable voice personas. Developers can integrate voice I/O into MCP-aware agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline) via a single `voicebox.speak` tool call, or build on a REST API and built-in MCP server. The app is built with Tauri and Rust for native performance, and runs on macOS (MLX/Metal), Windows (CUDA), Linux, AMD ROCm, and Docker—keeping all audio data and models on-device. Content creators, developers, and privacy-conscious professionals would use it to produce podcasts, narrate long-form text, dictate efficiently, or give AI agents a customizable voice.

**Product Description Text**:
> Syncular is an offline-first data synchronization framework that keeps an SQLite database on each client and reconciles changes through a server-owned commit log, enabling apps to read locally and continue working without connectivity. Writes update local state immediately, enter an outbox, and are validated by the server during sync, with a formally specified wire protocol verified by shared byte-level conformance tests across both TypeScript and Rust cores. The browser client uses SQLite on OPFS, while native platforms—Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, and Tauri—share the Rust core and native SQLite bindings. **Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Cubby Clipboard is a Windows 11 clipboard history replacement that addresses the limited memory of the built-in `Win+V` history by providing persistent, searchable, and private clipboard management. It captures text, HTML, RTF, and image clips, supports keyboard-first navigation with pinning, folders, filters, and per-app contexts, and uses the built-in Windows OCR engine to extract text from copied screenshots so they become searchable offline. Stored clipboard payloads are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a key tied to the current Windows user account, and the app contains no accounts, cloud sync, analytics, or telemetry, while it intentionally ignores file copy payloads since they reference paths rather than content. The desktop application is built with a Tauri shell combining a Rust backend (`src-tauri/`) that handles clipboard access, storage, windowing, and IPC with a React and TypeScript frontend (`frontend/`), targeting Windows 11 on both x64 and ARM64; the companion Cloudflare Pages marketing site lives in `product_pages/`. It is distributed under GPL-3.0 (derived from the PastePaw codebase) and is intended for Windows users, technical writers, support agents, developers, and privacy-conscious individuals who frequently copy and re-use text or images and want reliable local search across extended history, including inside pasted screenshots.

**Product Description Text**:
> Learn how to design large-scale systems. Prep for the system design interview. Includes Anki flashcards.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> The System Design Primer is a curated, open-source learning resource that addresses the challenge of designing scalable, large-scale systems—a required skill for technical interviews at many tech companies. It organizes scattered web resources into a structured curriculum covering core concepts like the CAP theorem, consistency patterns, load balancing, caching, sharding, microservices, and asynchronism, with each topic presented alongside pros, cons, and trade-off analyses. The repository includes practice system design and object-oriented design interview questions with sample solutions, discussions, code, and diagrams to help candidates prepare effectively. Anki flashcard decks for system design, system design exercises, and OO design exercises use spaced repetition to reinforce learning on the go. The guide is multilingual, with translations or translation efforts in over a dozen languages including English, Japanese, Chinese, Portuguese, German, and Spanish. It targets software engineers preparing for system design interviews and anyone seeking to deepen their understanding of distributed systems architecture, with content continually updated through community contributions.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Bootstrap is a popular front-end framework for building responsive, mobile-first websites and web applications. It provides prebuilt HTML, CSS, and JavaScript components that simplify layout, styling, interactive behavior, and consistent UI design. The framework includes responsive grid systems, utilities, navigation, forms, modals, tooltips, and other reusable interface elements. Developers can use compiled or source-based assets with support for minified files, source maps, Sass, RTL layouts, and JavaScript bundles that include Popper. Bootstrap is suitable for front-end developers, designers, and teams seeking to accelerate web development while maintaining cross-device compatibility. The repository supports installation through npm, Yarn, Bun, Composer, NuGet, and direct downloads, with documentation powered by Astro.

> An AI-powered design intelligence skill that generates professional, tailored UI/UX design systems on demand, eliminating the guesswork of choosing colors, typography, layout patterns, and effects for new projects. Its flagship Design System Generator uses a reasoning engine with 192 reasoning rules to analyze project requirements and run five parallel searches across product categories, UI styles, color palettes, landing page patterns, and typography pairings, then delivers a complete specification including anti-patterns to avoid and a pre-delivery accessibility checklist. Supporting 79 searchable UI styles with 50 actively maintained, it produces structured recommendations covering hero patterns, CTA placement, section ordering, and platform-appropriate interactions. Built in Python 3.x and distributed via npm (ui-ux-pro-max-cli), it targets frontend developers, designers, and AI-assisted coding workflows who need consistent, production-ready design decisions across multiple platforms and frameworks.

**Product Description Text**:
> A collection of DESIGN.md files analysis by popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Awesome DESIGN.md is a curated collection of plain-text design system documents extracted from real-world brand websites, covering AI platforms, developer tools, databases, productivity apps, and creative tools. Each DESIGN.md captures analyzed design tokens, typography, color palettes, spacing rules, and component patterns from brands like Vercel, Linear, Supabase, Notion, Cursor, and dozens more. Developers drop the file into their project root and instruct an AI coding agent to generate UI that visually matches the chosen brand's design language — no Figma exports or JSON schemas required. The concept builds on Google's Stitch DESIGN.md format, leveraging markdown as a format that LLMs parse natively for consistent, high-quality output. The repository is community-driven, regularly updated, and includes a request system for analyzing additional sites on demand. It targets developers, designers, and "vibecoders" who want production-ready aesthetic consistency when shipping AI-generated interfaces.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Storybook is an open-source frontend workshop that enables developers to build, document, and test UI components in isolation, separate from the main application. It solves the challenge of developing and validating components without needing to navigate through full app states, making UI development faster and more reliable. The tool supports a wide range of frameworks including React, Angular, Vue, Svelte, Preact, Ember, SolidJS, Qwik, HTML, and Web Components, with extensions for React Native, Android, iOS, and Flutter. It features a rich ecosystem of addons for component design, documentation, testing, and interactivity, with an extensible API for custom configurations. Trusted by thousands of teams, Storybook serves frontend developers, design system maintainers, and QA engineers seeking to create bulletproof, reusable UI components. Continuous integration is ensured through CircleCI builds and Codecov coverage, while an active community provides support via Discord and GitHub Discussions.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Screenshot-to-Code is an AI-powered tool that converts screenshots, mockups, Figma designs, and screen recordings into clean, functional front-end code, eliminating the tedious manual process of translating visual designs into markup. It supports multiple output stacks including HTML+Tailwind, HTML+CSS, React+Tailwind, Vue+Tailwind, Bootstrap, and Ionic+Tailwind, with optional video-to-prototype mode for recreating interactive websites from recordings. The app leverages leading AI models from OpenAI (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 Mini), Anthropic (Claude Opus 4.6/4.8), and Google (Gemini 3 Flash/3.1 Pro), along with Replicate for image generation, background removal, and asset extraction that reuses real logos and images from the source screenshot. The architecture consists of a React/Vite frontend paired with a FastAPI backend, supporting local development via Poetry or one-command deployment through Docker Compose, while a hosted version at screenshottocode.com offers immediate use without setup. Designers, front-end developers, and product teams will find it especially useful for rapidly prototyping from visual references, with configurable API keys enabling users to balance cost, quality, and provider preferences.

It solves the common challenge of implementing smooth, performant web animations without relying on heavy frameworks or complex CSS keyframes. Key features include a modular ES module architecture, built-in staggering and easing functions, looping and alternating playback, and support for multiple output formats (ESM, UMD, CJS, IIFE). The library is ideal for front-end developers and web designers building interactive UIs, animated marketing sites, or data visualizations. Maintained by Julian Garnier and distributed under the MIT license, it leverages modern JavaScript tooling with type declarations and a comprehensive development workflow including browser and Node testing.

**Product Description Text**:
> 🎨 Local-first, open-source Claude Design alternative. 🖥️ Native desktop app. ⚡ 259+ Skills · ✨ 142+ Design Systems 🖼️ Web · desktop · mobile prototypes · slides · images · videos · HyperFrames 📦 Sandboxed preview · HTML/PDF/PPTX/MP4 export 🤖 Claude Code / OpenClaw / Codex / Cursor / OpenCode / Qwen / Copilot / Hermes / Kimi & 17+ CLIs.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Open Design is an open-source, local-first desktop application that positions itself as a Claude Design alternative, turning existing coding agents into full design engines. It solves the problem of designing inside closed, vendor-locked tools by exposing the design process as a filesystem of functional skills, rendering templates, and brand-grade `DESIGN.md` design systems that agents can read, write, and remix. The app generates web, desktop, and mobile prototypes, dashboards, slides, documents, images, and HyperFrame motion graphics, with sandboxed iframe previews and native export to HTML, PDF, PPTX, and MP4. It supports DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`), Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and 20+ other CLI-based coding agents, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint via BYOK. **Product Description Text**:
> Fast, accurate & comprehensive text measurement & layout

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> **Pretext** is a pure JavaScript/TypeScript library that performs fast, accurate multiline text measurement and layout without ever touching the DOM. It solves the problem of expensive layout reflows triggered by calls like `getBoundingClientRect`, instead using its own measurement engine grounded in the browser's font metrics to compute paragraph heights, line counts, and individual line widths purely arithmetically.

The library exposes two main workflows: a simple `prepare` + `layout` pair for quickly determining a paragraph's total height and line count given a max width, and a richer segment-based API (`prepareWithSegments`, `layoutWithLines`, `walkLineRanges`, `layoutNextLineRange`) for manually laying out lines—useful for rendering to Canvas, SVG, WebGL, or server-side targets. It supports multilingual text including complex scripts (Chinese, Arabic, emoji), CSS-like options for `white-space`, `word-break`, and `letter-spacing`, soft-hyphen-based hyphenation, and a separate `rich-inline` helper for atomic inline items such as chips and mentions.

Pretext is aimed at web developers building virtualization, masonry layouts, dynamic reflow around floating elements, scroll anchoring, browser-free UI verification (especially AI-assisted iteration), and any scenario needing deterministic, reflow-free text metrics. It is distributed on npm as `@chenglou/pretext`, works across browsers, and is designed to extend to server-side rendering.

A distinctive feature is its optional cross-process separation between core logic and rendering, allowing the two to communicate via named pipes, HTTP, or MiniHTTP—useful for distributed applications and remote view models. The framework also offers unique coding-agent support by exposing UI Automation features through an HTTP server, enabling AI agents to operate the interface even when the screen is locked. With a rich control library, custom template system, multi-language FFI integration, and hosted mode for rendering multiple windows in a single native window, GacUI targets C++ developers building modern desktop applications that require both performance and architectural flexibility.

Because it is a standards-based custom element, it integrates with React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Solid, Qwik, HTMX, and plain HTML without framework-specific adapters. An optional `init` command auto-generates JSX type declarations for React, Solid, and Qwik and adds pre-hydration CSS for SSR frameworks like Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix, and Qwik, while leaving the codebase untouched when skipped (no postinstall hook runs).

- **Attached Keywords**: `design, svg, frontend, javascript`

**Product Description Text**:
> liquid-glass is a single-file, dependency-free JavaScript module that brings Apple's liquid-glass aesthetic to the web by making translucent panels actually bend the content behind them at their edges. It solves the problem of convincingly simulating refractive glass in CSS, where standard `backdrop-filter: blur()` produces only a flat frosted look. The technique uses an SVG `feDisplacementMap` filter driven by a canvas-generated displacement map (RGB ramps encoding X/Y offsets, neutralized in the interior so refraction is confined to a rim band), with three staggered per-channel passes combined via `feBlend` to produce a faint chromatic-aberration fringe. Real refraction is supported in Chromium browsers, while Safari and Firefox automatically fall back to a configurable frosted blur. Frontend developers building marketing sites, design portfolios, or app-style UIs can drop it onto any DOM element, tune parameters like `scale`, `chroma`, `border`, `mapBlur`, and `blur` via a simple options object, and rely on automatic resize handling plus a `destroy()` method for clean integration with frameworks like React.

The library maps a target hue onto these reference curves, ensuring the generated palette maintains similar accessible contrast ratios and vibrancy. It employs sophisticated scaling methods to adjust lightness and chroma, preserving the aesthetic integrity of the original design system. Furthermore, it supports custom ramps, allowing developers to define and integrate their own color scales for precise palette generation.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Slot-JSX is a custom JSX pragma designed to enable declarative, slottable components for implementing patterns like `asChild` and render function props. It fundamentally transforms the rendering process by replacing a component's root element with its child, preserving the component's internal structure. This approach eliminates the need for `React.cloneElement`, streamlining the React tree and improving composition. The library offers robust support for deeply nested slottables and is fully compatible with React Server Components and asynchronous components. Furthermore, it facilitates complex patterns, including render props, giving developers fine-grained control over element rendering. Slot-JSX provides a type-safe and composable foundation for building highly flexible UI components.

Terminal users, UI designers, and data-visualization developers who work under warm-screen filtering will benefit, with the deeper palettes intentionally trading color variety for survival of semantic distinctions at extreme color temperatures.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Hyalite is a single-file JavaScript library that simulates realistic refraction through a thick slab of bevelled glass on the web, without WebGL or a build step. It solves the problem that CSS `backdrop-filter` blur alone cannot bend straight lines or darken edges the way real glass does, by computing a per-element lens map that drives an SVG filter via `backdrop-filter: url(#…)`. The center stays clear while the bevel pulls the background inward, magnifies it, darkens along the rim, and catches a line of specular light; three bevel profiles (circle, squircle, lip) and chromatic dispersion are supported. Web developers who want premium "liquid glass" UI effects (cards, panels, overlays) without a graphics pipeline can drop in `hyalite.js`, style with `--hyalite` and `--hyalite-edge` custom properties, and tune behavior through a small API including `Hyalite.watch`, `Hyalite.attach`, `Hyalite.setOpts`, and live resizing via a `ResizeObserver` with coalesced rebuilds. The stack is pure vanilla JavaScript and CSS using SVG filters; it renders only in Chromium, while Safari, Firefox, and other browsers gracefully fall back to a plain blur. Three demo pages plus a Node-based headless test runner exercise asymmetric radii, elliptical corners, overlap rules, quarter symmetry, dispersion invariance, and resize/materialize animations.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Morphicons is a zero-dependency library that morphs any stroke-based icon into any other with spring physics, supporting Lucide, Tabler, Heroicons, Iconoir, or custom path data. It solves the dual problems of naive coordinate interpolation (which shears shapes mid-transition) and the tedious requirement to hand-declare rotation groups for congruent icon pairs like arrow-right → arrow-down, instead computing optimal 2D shape alignment via closed-form Procrustes analysis so rotations emerge naturally from the math. The library exposes unified bindings for React, Vue, Svelte, React Native, plus framework-agnostic Web Component and Astro shells, all sharing an identical API with three usage modes: uncontrolled (just change the prop), controlled (bind to external progress), and imperative (ref-based `morphTo` / `set`). It consumes icon *data* (`IconNode` or raw `d` strings from the vanilla `lucide` package) rather than framework-specific components, making it a drop-in replacement for `lucide-react` with full prop pass-through (`size`, `strokeWidth`, `color`, `className`, etc.) and accessible defaults (`aria-hidden` unless labeled, `role="img"` + `<title>` otherwise). SSR is clean—the server emits static SVG with zero flash—and morphs play regardless of OS reduce-motion by default, with an opt-in `reducedMotion="user"` mode.

Key features include physical rim lighting, chromatic dispersion for prismatic edges, spring-based motion primitives for press, bounce, drag, and mount animations, and droplet-style metaball merging for grouped elements. Designers and developers building premium interfaces—such as navigation bars, command palettes, tab indicators, floating controls, cards, sheets, and glassy buttons—can choose from six material presets (`clear`, `thin`, `regular`, `thick`, `ultra`, `adaptive`) and fine-tune properties like blur, refraction strength, index of refraction, and light angle. The engine emphasizes performance through refcounted, reusable displacement maps that are shared across same-size glass elements, with graceful degradation in non-Chromium browsers that retain frost, tint, shadow, and lighting layers. Distributed as a TypeScript-ready npm package (`quick-liquid`), it requires Node 18+ for builds and React 18+ only when using the React wrapper, with no stylesheet import required.

- **Primary Language**: `Not specified` | **Stars**: `★ 0` | **License**: `Unspecified / FOSS`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Github Awesome* | Video: *GitHub Trending Today #44: paritok, KiroCrew, wyzer, quickdraw, RunCat Neo, gemma-translator, auteur* | Published: *2026-08-09*
- **Attached Keywords**: `animation, ui, cross-platform, tools, react`

**Product Description Text**:
> `react-native-nitro-theme-transition` solves a limitation in React Native where theme changes happen atomically on the JavaScript thread, making smooth UI transitions impossible. It snapshots the current screen to the GPU, runs the user's synchronous theme-change callback underneath, then animates the snapshot away using the platform's native render-thread animators—Core Animation on iOS and the platform animators on Android—so a busy JS thread cannot drop frames. Five transition kinds are supported: circular reveal, inverse circular reveal, slide wipe, fade, and blur, all sharing a single timing curve so iOS and Android agree. The library is not a theming system itself; it works with any synchronous state change, including those driven by Unistyles, React Native's StyleSheet, or direct native writes. Built on Nitro Modules, it ships native code requiring an `expo prebuild` and rebuild, but gracefully degrades to an instant theme swap when the native module is missing.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> TSRX (TypeScript Render Extensions) is a TypeScript language extension that addresses the fragmentation of component development by keeping TypeScript setup, JSX-shaped structure, template control flow, and scoped styles together in unified `.tsrx` files. The language introduces statement containers (`@{ ... }`) that let local logic live in the same lexical scope as the rendered template, alongside template-native directives like `@if`, `@for`, `@switch`, and `@try` for declarative control flow, plus component-scoped `<style>` blocks with automatic class hashing. TSRX parses source into a framework-neutral AST and compiles to idiomatic output for multiple targets, including React, Preact, Solid, Vue, Ripple, and Octane, allowing new frameworks to be supported via standalone plugins. The repository ships the core compiler, target compilers, runtime helpers, build integrations for Vite, Rspack, Turbopack, and Bun, plus Prettier, ESLint, TypeScript, and language-server tooling, with editor support for VS Code, Zed, Neovim, IntelliJ, and Sublime Text. Currently in active beta, TSRX targets front-end developers who want a single, typed authoring experience across multiple UI frameworks without sacrificing the idioms of their chosen runtime.

> apple-liquid-glass-webgl is a framework-free WebGL2 library that recreates Apple's translucent "liquid glass" surfaces directly in the browser. It solves the problem of rendering high-fidelity, real-time glass effects (screen-space refraction, variable blur, Fresnel reflection, chromatic dispersion, edge highlights, contact shadows) without relying on CSS hacks or platform-specific APIs, and ships two independent renderers side by side: a frosted V1 model (`LiquidGlassWebGL`) and a clear optical V2 model (`LiquidGlassWebGLV2`) that can be instantiated together to compare or combine styles.

The library supports four built-in shapes — folders, rounded rectangles, pills, and circles — accepts CSS-pixel coordinates, and exposes fully customizable material parameters (corner roundness, bevel, refraction, blur, lighting, edge highlights, tint) with safe defaults returned as fresh copies so applications can tweak them without mutating shared state. It auto-scales optical features when a component's short side is too small for its configured bevel, caping the refracting rim at 30% of that side and proportionally adjusting glass height, blur, and highlights.

Web developers building UI demos, design systems, interactive prototypes, or web applications that want iOS/macOS-style glass aesthetics will find it most useful; installation is a simple `npm install apple-liquid-glass-webgl`, and runtime support can be checked via `LiquidGlassWebGL.isSupported()` to gracefully fall back to CSS

#### 1. [rustdesk](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk) (`rustdesk/rustdesk`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://rustdesk.com](https://rustdesk.com)
- **Primary Language**: `Rust` | **Stars**: `★ 121,094` | **License**: `AGPL-3.0`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Cooly* | Video: *Cooly's Chrome Links* | Published: *2026-09-02*
- **Attached Keywords**: `rust, cross-platform, collaboration, self-hosted, alternatives, desktop`
- **GitHub Topics**: `android, anydesk, dart, flatpak, flutter, flutter-apps, ios, linux, macos, p2p, rdp, remote-control, remote-desktop, rust`

**Product Description Text**:
> An open-source remote desktop application designed for self-hosting, as an alternative to TeamViewer.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> RustDesk is an open-source remote desktop application written in Rust, designed as a self-hostable alternative to TeamViewer. It addresses privacy and data control concerns by allowing users to either use the project's public rendezvous/relay servers or deploy their own infrastructure, ensuring no third party can access their remote sessions. Key features include out-of-the-box functionality with no configuration required, cross-platform support (Windows, Linux, macOS, and mobile via F-Droid and Flathub), and a GUI built with Flutter (with Sciter support deprecated). The technology stack leverages Rust for core functionality alongside C++ libraries managed via vcpkg for video codecs (libvpx, aom), audio (opus), and image processing (libyuv), with screen capture handled through custom Rust libraries. It is intended for individuals, businesses, and IT professionals seeking a secure, controllable remote access solution without dependence on commercial services.


#### 2. [Deep-Live-Cam](https://github.com/hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam) (`hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam](https://github.com/hacksider/Deep-Live-Cam)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://deeplivecam.net/](https://deeplivecam.net/)
- **Primary Language**: `Python` | **Stars**: `★ 94,297` | **License**: `AGPL-3.0`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *ManuAGI - AutoGPT Tutorials* | Video: *Top Dev Tool Projects : Langfuse, Shannon, Temporal, OpenMetadata & CodeBurn* | Published: *2026-04-23*
- **Attached Keywords**: `python, video, ai`
- **GitHub Topics**: `ai, ai-deep-fake, ai-face, ai-webcam, artificial-intelligence, deep-fake, deepfake, deepfake-webcam, faceswap, fake-webcam, gan, real-time-deepfake, realtime, realtime-deepfake`

**Product Description Text**:
> real time face swap and one-click video deepfake with only a single image (uncensored)

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Deep-Live-Cam enables real-time face swapping and one-click video deepfake creation using just a single source image, eliminating the need for extensive training data or complex model preparation. The tool supports live webcam feeds as well as pre-recorded video processing, making it accessible for streaming, content creation, and entertainment purposes such as creating personalized movie experiences, memes, or live performances. Key features include a Mouth Mask function to preserve natural lip movement, multi-face mapping for swapping different faces onto multiple subjects simultaneously, and built-in content moderation checks that block nudity, graphic material, and sensitive footage before processing. The project provides optimized pre-built binaries for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), and CPU-only environments, with optional GPU acceleration through CUDA for Nvidia hardware. It targets content creators, streamers, meme artists, and developers in the AI-generated media industry while requiring GPU support (NVIDIA/AMD/Apple Silicon) for optimal real-time performance. The tech stack leverages ONNX-based face-swapping models (inswapper_128_fp16), GFPGANv1.4 for face enhancement, PyTorch, and ONNX Runtime execution providers, with Python 3.14 as the recommended runtime.

**Product Description Text**:
> generating videos, OmniRoute for routing AI provider requests with auto-fallback, and CapRover for self-hosted app deployment without manual Docker setup

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> MoneyPrinterTurbo is an open-source AI-powered short video generator that automates the entire video creation pipeline from a single topic or keyword. It leverages large language models (such as Kimi K3, DeepSeek, Doubao, and GPT) to write video scripts, extract search keywords for relevant footage, generate subtitles, and select background music, before synthesizing everything into a high-definition short video. The tool provides both a WebUI and an API interface, making it accessible to non-technical users while remaining flexible for developers, and it supports batch video generation as well as integration with various multimodal AI services for image, audio, and video generation. The fully automated workflow makes it well suited for content creators, social media marketers, and educators who need to produce short-form video content at scale without manual editing. Built primarily in Python and packaged with cross-platform support, it lowers the barrier to AI-driven video production by eliminating the need to stitch together multiple tools or possess video editing expertise.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> implements a real-time voice cloning system designed to generate arbitrary speech from a cloned voice within five seconds. It is based on the SV2TTS framework, which transfers knowledge from speaker verification tasks to multispeaker text-to-speech synthesis. The system utilizes a deep learning approach involving stages for creating a digital voice representation, generating speech from text, and employing a real-time vocoder. Built using Python, PyTorch, and TensorFlow, the project integrates established models like Tacotron and WaveRNN for efficient audio synthesis. This implementation provides a complete, end-to-end deep learning solution for high-quality, real-time voice cloning.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> imgproxy is a fast and secure standalone HTTP server designed to handle image resizing, processing, and conversion on the fly, serving as a drop-in replacement for in-application image processing code. It solves the problem of repeatedly re-preparing images for changing designs by processing them on demand through specially crafted URLs, offloading work from web applications. Key features include support for multiple formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, and more), operations like resizing, cropping, rotating, watermarking, and filtering, plus optimizations such as metadata stripping and PNG quantization. Built on the libvips image processing library, imgproxy prioritizes speed, minimal memory footprint, and security measures like image bomb prevention, URL signing, and source restrictions. Web developers and teams managing large-scale image-heavy platforms use imgproxy to streamline their image pipelines, with deployment made simple via a single Docker command. A commercial version, imgproxy Pro, extends the open-source offering with advanced features such as video and PDF previews, object detection, and SSIM-based quality optimization.

> Semantic search over videos using Gemini Embedding 2.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> SentrySearch enables semantic search over video footage, allowing users to type natural-language queries (e.g., "red truck running a stop sign") and receive a trimmed clip from the source file. It works by splitting videos into overlapping chunks, embedding each chunk using Google's Gemini Embedding API, Alibaba DashScope (Qwen Cloud), or a local Qwen3-VL model, and storing the resulting vectors in a local ChromaDB database for fast similarity matching. The tool supports text queries, image-based queries for visual similarity, configurable chunk durations and overlap, optional VLM-based re-ranking, deduplication of near-identical results, and automatic clip trimming with confidence thresholds. It is designed for users managing large volumes of footage—dashcam owners, security researchers, content creators, or investigators—who need to locate specific events quickly without manually scrubbing through hours of video. The pipeline extends to companion tools (SentryMerge for multi-cam stitching and SentryBlur for redaction), forming a broader surveillance and footage-analysis workflow. SentrySearch is a CLI tool built on Python 3.11/3.12, installable via `uv`, and relies on ffmpeg for video processing and either cloud APIs or a local PyTorch-based model as its embedding backend.

**Product Description Text**:
> claude-real-video solves the problem of letting LLMs actually *see* video content rather than just reading transcripts. It extracts scene-aware keyframes from a URL or local file, deduplicates near-identical frames using a sliding window, and transcribes audio locally — producing a clean folder of frames plus a transcript that any LLM can ingest. All processing runs on the user's machine, with no uploads required during analysis. Key features include a `crv` CLI and a no-terminal `crv-web` UI, adaptive sampling for slow-changing content, text-anchor frame forcing for lecture-style videos, and optional speaker diarization for multi-speaker content. It works as a standalone keyframe extractor without any ML models, and integrates with coding agents via a one-command skills install for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 50+ compatible hosts. It's built on Python with PySceneDetect for scene-change detection, OpenCV/ImageHash for perceptual deduplication, Whisper for transcription, and pyannote for speaker diarization. The package is MIT-licensed and provides benchmarked results showing significant token savings — a 3-minute test kept 170 frames versus 180 from naive extraction, with a v0.7.16 fix ensuring small fast-moving subjects are no longer missed by the dedup comparator.

> TADA is an open-source speech-language model framework designed for high-fidelity speech generation and synthesis. It achieves a unified stream by aligning speech and text through a novel Text-Acoustic Dual Alignment mechanism. TADA employs dynamic duration synthesis, where each autoregressive step generates the speech duration and prosody corresponding to a single text token. By synchronizing the modalities at a 1:1 token level, TADA significantly reduces computational overhead compared to traditional models. It leverages a unified architecture built on Llama 3.2 to deliver efficient and reliable speech modeling.

The method propagates the first frame's features along user-specified point trajectories to guide video generation, producing 5-second 480p videos with state-of-the-art motion controllability comparable to commercial systems such as Kling 1.5 Pro's Motion Brush. The release also ships MoveBench, a curated benchmark with diverse content, longer video durations, and high-quality trajectory annotations. Backbone: Wan-I2V-14B; framework: PyTorch (>=2.4.0); supporting tools include CoTracker, umt5-xxl, and HuggingFace; acceleration via FSDP and xDiT USP for multi-GPU inference; ComfyUI and Wan2GP wrappers support low-VRAM usage. **Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> rCM introduces a novel framework for scaling up continuous-time consistency distillation methods, such as sCM and MeanFlow, to large-scale video diffusion models. The work utilizes a Score-Regularized approach combined with JVP-based diffusion distillation to enhance both the quality and diversity of generated videos. A key innovation is the forward–reverse divergence joint distillation, which effectively complements traditional distillation methods by addressing the quality bottleneck in consistency models. Furthermore, rCM provides an open-sourced FlashAttention-2 Jacobian-vector product kernel, enabling efficient parallelization for large-scale training. This methodology allows for state-of-the-art video generation in only a few steps, significantly improving generation efficiency.

- **Primary Language**: `TypeScript` | **Stars**: `★ 474` | **License**: `NOASSERTION`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Cooly* | Video: *Cooly's Chrome Links* | Published: *2026-09-02*
- **Attached Keywords**: `audio, speech-recognition, nextjs, video, electron`
- **GitHub Topics**: `audio, media, media-editing, media-editor, transcribe, transcription, video, video-editing, video-editor, video-processing`

**Product Description Text**:
> Rescript is an open-source, transcript-based media editor that lets users cut video and audio by editing text — deleting words in an automatically generated transcript removes the corresponding segments from the source media. It solves the problem of tedious timeline-based editing by providing a familiar, text-style interface while keeping all processing fully on-device for privacy, with no uploads or accounts required. Key features include local Whisper-based transcription with word-level timestamps, speaker diarization, one-click filler and silence removal, a draggable waveform/wordbar timeline, frame-accurate re-encoding via ffmpeg.wasm, and export to MP4/WebM, M4A/MP3/WAV, and SRT/VTT/JSON. The tool is aimed at podcasters, content creators, journalists, and anyone who wants fast, non-destructive cuts without uploading footage to a server. The stack combines Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind for the UI, Electron for the signed macOS/Windows/Linux desktop builds, transformers.js (with WebGPU/WASM fallback) for Whisper inference, pyannote for speaker labels, ffmpeg.wasm for media handling, and zustand for state management. The software is available both as a browser app and a desktop download, licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Rescript is an open-source, transcript-based video and audio editor that runs entirely in the browser or as a desktop app, letting users cut media by editing text rather than manipulating a timeline. Users drop in a file, which is transcribed locally with Whisper for word-level timestamps and pyannote for speaker labels; deleting words in the transcript removes the corresponding clip, with options for one-click filler and silence removal. The tool appeals to podcasters, video creators, and interviewers who want a fast, text-driven editing workflow without uploading sensitive media to a server. Export is handled locally via ffmpeg.wasm, producing frame-accurate MP4/WebM video (up to 4K), audio (M4A/MP3/WAV), or subtitle files, with users also able to import SRT/VTT/JSON transcripts to bypass transcription entirely. Built as a Next.js/React/TypeScript app with Tailwind and zustand for state, it ships as a cross-platform Electron desktop build and a Chromium-based web app that works offline after initial model download. The project is licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial, restricting commercial use without author permission.

VAP leverages a reference video as a direct semantic prompt to guide the generation process. This work aims to advance the field of controllable video synthesis.

**Product Description Text**:
> SparkVSR: Interactive Video Super-Resolution via Sparse Keyframe Propagation

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> SparkVSR is an interactive framework designed for Video Super-Resolution (VSR) that utilizes sparse keyframes as an expressive control signal. The method allows users to super-resolve a small set of keyframes and then propagate these priors across the entire video sequence while maintaining adherence to the original low-resolution motion. It employs a keyframe-conditioned latent-pixel two-stage training pipeline to fuse low-resolution and high-resolution latents, ensuring robust cross-space propagation. During inference, the model supports flexible keyframe selection and reference-free guidance for superior restoration quality. Experiments demonstrate improved temporal consistency and strong restoration, outperforming baselines on key video quality benchmarks. This approach establishes SparkVSR as a generic, keyframe-driven framework applicable to various video processing tasks.

- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Github Awesome* | Video: *GitHub Trending Weekly #40: clawk, clodex-ide, neverclick, grok-build, Krbn, domain-sdk, Flawless* | Published: *2026-07-16*
- **Attached Keywords**: `image-generation, rust, python, inference, computer-vision`

**Product Description Text**:
> Pixel Art Fixer converts fake "pixel art" — images that merely look like pixel art but contain off-grid cells, non-integer scales, anti-aliased mush, or bloated resolutions — into true, grid-aligned pixel art at its native resolution. It uses pure image processing (no neural network required) to recover the underlying pseudo-pixel grid by combining three phase-invariant detectors (autocorrelation, run-length combs, shift self-similarity) and arbitrating disagreements through a fused evidence stack of spectral, tile-Rayleigh, variance, and round-trip distillability signals. Reconstruction decouples placement from color: a small adaptive quantization decides crisp structure while final colors are sampled from the original un-quantized pixels, preserving rare hues and accents without smearing. A benchmark of 100 source images across 43 distortion categories shows it recovers the exact native resolution on 77% of inputs (versus under 5% for competing tools) with 94% grid alignment and a mean CIELAB color error of ~1.6 when correct. The repository ships both a Python reference implementation (numpy, scipy, OpenCV, Pillow) and a dependency-free Rust binary that runs 11–24x faster at lower memory, aimed at pixel artists, game developers, and tool builders who need to recover editable, palette-swappable sprites from AI-generated or upscaled sources.

Photographers can browse multiple folder roots without importing into a managed library, with real-time FSEvents-based monitoring and Spotlight-backed search keeping the workspace responsive. > VibeClip is an open-source, self-hosted AI video editor that automatically converts long videos—podcasts, interviews, talks, or streams—into vertical, captioned 9:16 shorts ready for social platforms. The pipeline transcribes audio locally with faster-whisper, uses an LLM to score the strongest moments by hook, flow, and value (rather than simple keywords), then reframes clips around the speaker and burns word-synced captions with ffmpeg. A tool-calling chat agent lets users refine every aspect of a clip through natural-language commands like "make clip 2 punchier" or "add a zoom at 0:05," applying trims, filler-word removal, zooms, styles, music, b-roll, and brand overlays—with a one-step undo for multi-step edits. Built-in styles (hormozi, mrbeast, podcast_minimal, kinetic) apply captions, pace, and effects together, while custom JSON presets are supported, all rendered through a web studio UI featuring a live 9:16 preview, clip cards, CapCut-style timeline, and embedded chat copilot. Designed for content creators, editors, and marketers who want privacy and control, it operates on a bring-your-own-key model with no vendor proxying—supporting OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter), with keys encrypted at rest per user. Deployment is a single `docker compose up` command (or local Python install) requiring only one LLM key, and the AGPL-3.0 license ensures no SaaS lock-in for self-hosters.

It targets developers, founders, and AI-assisted creators who want to produce launch videos, branded clips, LinkedIn loops, or remakes of reference launch videos (including a "remake mode" that extracts frames, detects cuts, and rebuilds a 1:1 brand version) using only free, open tooling. **Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> **effect-mq** — Effect-native background job processing for TypeScript

A schema-first job queue built on [Effect](https://effect.website) v4 that brings the proven semantics of BullMQ — retries, repeatable schedules, deduplication, and worker runtimes — into Effect's typed, structured-concurrency world. Jobs are defined as class schemas with payloads, success types, idempotency keys, and retry defaults baked in, eliminating string-based handler lookup and untyped payloads.

The package splits into tree-shakeable modules: `effect-mq` for the storage-agnostic core, `drizzle-postgres` for a Drizzle-native Postgres store with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claims, `redis` for an atomic-Lua Redis backend, and `testing` for conformance drivers. Every attempt is persisted in a run ledger, dedup, throttle, debounce, and cross-process cancellation work with Effect fibers, and metrics integrate with the Effect `Metric` system. Drizzle-kit owns migrations because the job tables are plain schema factories users re-export.

Teams already running Effect services that need durable, observable background work — email sends, image processing, scheduled data pipelines — get compile-time wiring of stores to jobs, runtime safety from `Schema.Redacted`, and the same control primitives (`timeout`, `interrupt`, `pause`) they use elsewhere in their app.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> SimFoundry is a modular, automated pipeline that converts short real-world videos into physics-ready simulation scenes in under an hour, eliminating the need for manual 3D annotation. It solves the costly and labor-intensive problem of creating realistic simulation environments for robotics policy training by performing object segmentation, geometry reconstruction, and textured mesh generation automatically, then compiling the results into OmniGibson-compatible scenes with physical parameters, digital cousin variations, and task proposals. The system is organized into three pipelines: Reconstruction (A), which runs 13 stages from video processing to USD export; Augmentation (B), which generates object/scene variations and task proposals; and Application (C), which loads scenes into OmniGibson for policy evaluation and teleoperation. Its fully modular architecture means every stage is an independently swappable component, so the pipeline improves as underlying foundation models advance—currently leveraging SAM3, DINOv3, Hunyuan3D, and Google's Gemini VLM. Robotics researchers and ML engineers working on sim-to-real transfer, imitation learning, or policy evaluation will find it particularly valuable, especially given the upcoming features for automated background generation and robotics data generation/training. The stack requires an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA, roughly 250 GB of disk space, and integrates with Hugging Face and Google Cloud Vertex AI services.

Built on top of the **HyperFrames** HTML + GSAP rendering engine plus **ffmpeg** for audio, it enforces a strict `init → preview → lint → render → verify` pipeline and produces a beat-by-beat `edit-report.md` for every edit. Installation is a single `npx vertical-video-editing-skill` command, and the target users are creators, agencies, and developers building automated video pipelines who need polished, on-brand output rather than uniform template-driven results.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> wrtag is a fast, automated music tagging and organisation tool that matches audio files against the MusicBrainz database, applies accurate metadata, and arranges them into a user-defined filesystem layout such as `Artist/(Year) Album/Track.ext`. Written in Go for performance, it positions itself as a simpler, more composable alternative to tools like Beets and MusicBrainz Picard, with a Unix-style suite including a command-line tool, a web interface (`wrtagweb`) for remote importing, and a `metadata` utility. Key features include cover art fetching from the Cover Art Archive, multi-disc release handling, ReplayGain calculation, lyrics retrieval, user-defined subprocess addons, and a `sync` subcommand for bulk re-tagging an existing library to reflect MusicBrainz updates. It supports safe concurrent processing via tree-style filesystem locking, reflink copies on supported filesystems, and runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows with static binaries or Docker images. wrtag is aimed at music collectors and self-hosted media library maintainers who want a consistent, validated, and scriptable workflow for keeping large music libraries accurately tagged.

It is a fork of youtube-dl based on the now-inactive youtube-dlc, and includes numerous new features, bug fixes, and quality-of-life improvements over its predecessors. The tool supports a wide range of functionality including format selection, subtitle extraction, SponsorBlock integration, post-processing options, video metadata modification, geo-restriction bypass, and authentication handling. It offers extensive configuration options through command-line flags or configuration files, and includes a plugin system for extending its capabilities with custom extractors and post-processors. yt-dlp is written in Python and can be installed via standalone binaries for Windows, macOS, and Linux, through pip, or from source. It is used by power users, archivists, developers building media-related tools, and anyone needing automated, programmatic access to online video and audio content.

**Product Description Text**:
> Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition system that tackles multilingual transcription, speech translation, and language identification through a single Transformer sequence-to-sequence model trained on a large, weakly supervised corpus. It addresses the brittleness of traditional multi-stage approaches by unifying speech processing tasks as token sequences decoded by the model, using task specifier tokens to switch between transcription, translation, and voice activity detection. The library is available in six model sizes ranging from 39M to 1550M parameters, including English-only variants and a faster "turbo" version, allowing users to balance accuracy against memory requirements (roughly 1–10 GB VRAM) and inference speed. It exposes both a command-line interface and a Python API for transcribing audio files, automatically handling audio loading via ffmpeg and padding input to 30-second sliding windows for autoregressive decoding. Developers, researchers, and product teams integrating speech-to-text, subtitling, or translation features into their applications would use Whisper, built on Python 3.8–3.11, PyTorch, and OpenAI's tiktoken tokenizer.
